title: Impact of Auxiliary Task Heterogeneity on Dose Prediction: A Controlled Study of Optimization Coupling and Dose Outcomes.
abstract: Background Auxiliary-task training has been increasingly explored in radiotherapy dose prediction to incorporate planning-relevant priors, such as patient anatomy, beam geometry, and spatial information, into model optimization. However, when auxiliary tasks differ in their physical meaning, input representation, and prediction target, their roles cannot be adequately understood from final prediction performance alone. Particularly in auxiliary-supervision frameworks without shared feature representations, it remains unclear whether an auxiliary task establishes an effective optimization connection with the primary network, actually uses the additional information provided to it, and produces stable performance effects. Purpose The purpose of this study was to compare heterogeneous auxiliary tasks for left-sided breast IMRT dose prediction under controlled conditions and to evaluate their relationships with the primary dose-prediction task in terms of optimization coupling, information use, and performance robustness. Materials and methods We implemented an independently parameterized auxiliary-supervised joint optimization framework comprising a primary 3D dose prediction network and three auxiliary networks targeting patient anatomy, beam geometry, and isocenter-related spatial information, without shared encoders or intermediate features. Specifically, we evaluated a dose-only baseline (DS) and four auxiliary-supervision configurations combining dose prediction with beam-geometry (BS), center-related (CS), patient-structure (PS), or all auxiliary supervision (AS). Using data from 30 patients, we generated 130 plans per patient via bounded perturbations of beam angles and isocenter position, and evaluated all configurations on 650 test plans from held-out patients under identical training settings. Prediction performance was first assessed using voxel-wise errors and dosimetric endpoints. Gradient analysis was then used to quantify direct optimization coupling between auxiliary losses and DoseNet, while a matched CT + predicted-dose versus CT-only input ablation evaluated the use of predicted-dose information by the Beam and Center tasks. Finally, performance robustness was assessed across multiple random seeds and under composite-loss and MSE-only primary dose objectives. Results DS achieved the lowest overall MAE/RMSE, while BS showed comparable performance: under the composite-loss setting, BS exhibited more consistent cross-seed improvements across several clinically relevant dosimetric endpoints. Further analyses revealed distinct pathways among the auxiliary tasks. Both Beam and Center were directly connected to DoseNet through the predicted dose, but Beam showed substantially larger relative gradient magnitudes, and inclusion of the predicted dose improved Beam prediction across all three random seeds. In contrast, Center showed no consistent benefit from predicted-dose information, while Patient had no direct auxiliary-gradient pathway to DoseNet. Changing the primary dose objective from the composite loss to MSE-only substantially altered the endpoint-level effects and cross-seed consistency of the auxiliary configurations, with the most pronounced loss of consistency observed for BS. Conclusion The role of auxiliary supervision cannot be determined from final performance changes alone. Optimization coupling, information use, and performance robustness represent distinct dimensions that should be evaluated separately. Gradient analysis, input ablation, performance comparisons across random seeds and primary loss formulations together provide a more complete framework for evaluating auxiliary supervision than performance comparison alone.

title: Comparative assessment of respiratory-induced tumor motion using fluoroscopy and four-dimensional CT of solitary pulmonary lesions.
abstract: Background Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is widely used to quantify respiratory-induced tumor motion in thoracic radiotherapy. However, 4DCT captures discretized respiratory phases and assumes stable breathing, potentially introducing reconstruction-related uncertainties. Fluoroscopy enables real-time observation across multiple breathing cycles, yet direct large-scale comparisons between fluoroscopy- and 4DCT-derived motion measurements remain scarce. Purpose To directly compare respiratory-induced tumor motion measured by fluoroscopy and 4DCT in patients with solitary pulmonary lesions undergoing proton therapy planning under free breathing without abdominal compression. Methods This retrospective study included 191 patients with solitary pulmonary lesions who underwent sequential fluoroscopy and 4DCT under free-breathing conditions as part of proton therapy planning. Tumor motion was evaluated in the craniocaudal direction and stratified by lung lobe. Furthermore, diaphragmatic motion was analyzed in 131 cases. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient was used to assess correlations between motions measured by the two modalities. Measurement differences were defined as ΔD (4DCT minus fluoroscopy) and analyzed according to fluoroscopy-measured respiratory displacement. For subgroup analyses, cases were categorized into < 5 mm, ≥ 5 to ≤ 10 mm, and > 10 mm motion groups based on fluoroscopy-measured respiratory displacement. For Bland-Altman analyses, motion magnitude was defined as the mean of the fluoroscopy- and 4DCT-derived respiratory displacement measurements, and intermodality agreement was assessed within each motion category. Results The correlation coefficients for tumor motion in the upper-, middle-, and lower-lobes were 0.61 (p < 0.01), 0.76 (p < 0.01), and 0.55 (p < 0.01), respectively. The corresponding correlation coefficients for diaphragmatic motion were lower: 0.40 (p < 0.01) on the left and 0.38 (p < 0.01) on the right. The median |ΔD| values (interquartile range) were 1.3 mm (0.7-1.9 mm), 2.4 mm (1.0-4.1 mm), and 4.7 mm (2.6-6.8 mm) for the < 5 mm, ≥ 5 to ≤ 10 mm, and > 10 mm groups, respectively. Overall, the mean difference between 4DCT and fluoroscopy was small (-0.2 mm; 95% confidence interval, -0.9 to 0.6 mm), with 95% limits of agreement of -10.2 to 9.9 mm. The limits of agreement widened with increasing respiratory motion. Conclusions In this single-institution study of patients undergoing proton therapy planning, respiratory motion measurements derived from fluoroscopy and 4DCT showed larger absolute differences for lower-lobe tumors (median |ΔD| = 4.20 mm) than for upper- and middle-lobe tumors (1.70 and 1.90 mm, respectively). These findings indicate that respiratory motion estimated by 4DCT alone should be interpreted with caution in such cases. When feasible and when the lesion is fluoroscopically visible, fluoroscopic assessment may serve as a useful consistency check to complement 4DCT-based motion evaluation.

title: Implementation of a 0.55T MR simulator for intracranial stereotactic radiosurgery.
abstract: Background Low-field MRI has several advantages for radiation therapy simulation. The reduced field strength lowers susceptibility artifacts near metallic implants, decreases intrinsic geometric distortion, and improves safety through lower SAR, reduced projectile risk, and fewer device interactions. MRI is the imaging foundation for SRS target delineation, and initial low-field MRI feasibility for brain radiotherapy planning has been demonstrated in small cohorts. However, SRS clinical implementation has not been reported. We describe the implementation of a 0.55T MR simulator and characterize lesion conspicuity across 102 lesions in 13 patients with multiple brain metastases, drawn from 211 consecutive SRS patients treated to 511 lesions over 12 months. Purpose To describe the clinical implementation of a 0.55T MR simulator (MAGNETOM Free.Max RT Edition, Siemens Healthineers) as a dedicated radiation therapy simulation system, following a systematic framework of acceptance testing per AAPM TG-284, longitudinal quality assurance, and SRS MRI protocol optimization. Methods Acceptance testing and commissioning followed AAPM TG-284 recommendations. Testing included the use of vendor-provided homogeneous phantoms, the ACR large phantom, and a commercially available large-field geometric distortion phantom. Longitudinal quality assurance was performed over a 12-month period using the ACR large phantom. Measured parameters included geometric accuracy, percent image uniformity (PIU), percent signal ghosting, low contrast detectability (LCD), and SNR. Contrast to noise ratio (CNR) was calculated for the lesions of a subset of SRS patients having 4 or greater metastatic lesions to evaluate the conspicuity of small SRS lesions in this challenging environment. Results All acceptance testing met TG-284 recommendations. Central frequency and transmitter gain were stable with changes of less than 0.01% and 0.3%, respectively, over the first month of testing. Geometric distortion after vendor 3D corrections measured less than 1 mm within 10 cm and less than 2 mm within 20 cm of isocenter. Monthly phantom testing over 12 months confirmed geometric stability within established tolerances. A brain imaging protocol achieved 1 mm slice thickness on 3D T1-weighted acquisitions consistent with ISRS guidelines, with total scan time under 35 minutes. To date, 211 intracranial SRS patients have been scanned and treated to a total of 511 lesions with a median volume of 0.58cc [0.004 - 304.48 cc]. The median CNR for the 102 lesions in the set of 13 patients with 4 or greater metastatic lesions was calculated as 6.81 [1.7-16.9] with only two lesions having a CNR < 2. Conclusions These findings support the feasibility of 0.55T MRI as a dedicated RT simulator capable of meeting the imaging demands of intracranial SRS. Formal comparative studies against higher field systems are needed before low-field imaging can be considered a standalone replacement for SRS planning.

title: Deep learning reconstruction for low-dose thoracic CT of calcification inserts: A phantom study of CNR, noise magnitude, and noise texture.
abstract: Purpose To compare filtered back projection (FBP), 50% Adaptive Statistical Iterative Reconstruction-Veo (ASiR), and medium-strength deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) for hydroxyapatite calcification inserts under different dose, tube-voltage, and phantom-size conditions using contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), background noise magnitude, and noise power spectrum (NPS) analysis. Methods A QRM-Thorax containing a QRM-CCI D100 cardiac calcification insert was scanned on a GE Revolution Apex CT system using institution-defined routine and low-dose protocols at 80, 100, 120, and 140 kVp, with and without an Extension Ring L. Images were reconstructed at 2.5-mm thickness using FBP, ASiR, and DLIR. CNR was evaluated for 3- and 5-mm inserts at 200, 400, and 800 mg HA/cm 3 . Background noise was assessed from a calcification-excluded mask. For NPS analysis, 10 calcification-free images were analyzed for each acquisition condition. Total two-dimensional NPS power, power-weighted normalized radial NPS, and power-weighted mean spatial frequency were calculated. Results DLIR reduced background noise magnitude and increased CNR relative to FBP across the evaluated conditions, whereas differences relative to ASiR varied with insert size, density, tube voltage, and phantom size. Across all 16 protocol, phantom-size, and tube-voltage combinations, ASiR and DLIR reduced total 2D NPS power by 58.1% and 75.8%, respectively, relative to FBP; DLIR reduced total power by 41.9% relative to ASiR. ASiR produced a more consistent shift toward lower power-weighted mean spatial frequencies, averaging 12.4% below FBP, whereas the shift with DLIR was smaller and more condition dependent, averaging 3.2% below FBP. Conclusions In this controlled phantom study, DLIR reduced total noise power and improved CNR relative to FBP, but its incremental difference from ASiR was task and protocol dependent. CNR and noise magnitude should be interpreted together with NPS because nonlinear reconstruction methods can alter both noise magnitude and spatial-frequency distribution.

title: Dose‑dependent image quality behavior of recently introduced clinical deep learning CT reconstruction methods.
abstract: Background Deep learning reconstruction (DLR) algorithms are increasingly used in CT to reduce image noise and support radiation dose reduction. However, DLR methods may alter spatial resolution and noise texture depending on dose level, reconstruction kernel, matrix size, and vendor implementation. Purpose To characterize how decreasing radiation dose affects noise magnitude, noise texture, and task-based spatial resolution for two recently available clinical CT deep learning reconstruction algorithms: Canon Precise IQ Engine (PIQE) super-resolution DLR and GE HealthCare TrueFidelity DLR. Methods The American College of Radiology CT accreditation phantom was scanned on an Aquilion ONE/INSIGHT Edition scanner (Canon Medical Systems USA) and a Revolution Apex scanner (GE HealthCare) across 12 dose levels. CTDIvol ranged from 0.7 to 20.0 mGy for Canon and from 0.68 to 20.46 mGy for GE. Canon images were reconstructed using filtered back projection (FBP) with a 512 matrix and PIQE Levels 1-3 with Body, Lung, and Cardiac kernels using a 1024 matrix. GE images were reconstructed using FBP and TrueFidelity low, medium, and high strengths with Standard, Lung, Bone, and Bone Plus kernels using a 512 matrix. Task-based spatial resolution was evaluated using the task transfer function (TTF). Noise magnitude and texture were evaluated using the noise power spectrum (NPS), including the Noise Magnitude Ratio (NMR), defined as the square root of the ratio of NPS areas between the DLR and the FBP reference, and the Central Frequency Ratio (CFR), defined as the ratio of the center of gravity of the NPS between DLR and FBP, reflecting noise texture shifts. Results At a high-dose comparison of 16.0 mGy for Canon and 16.43 mGy for GE, PIQE produced kernel-dependent changes in bone TTF50% relative to matched FBP, ranging from a 21.3% decrease to a 83.6% increase across kernels and DLR strengths. TrueFidelity increased bone TTF50% relative to matched FBP moderately across all evaluated kernels and strengths, with changes ranging from 3.7% to 14.7%. As dose decreased, PIQE TTF50% and TTF10% decreased substantially across evaluated kernels and inserts, whereas TrueFidelity TTF values remained relatively stable. PIQE produced lower NMR values than TrueFidelity. With decreasing dose, PIQE also demonstrated decreasing NMR and CFR values, indicating greater relative noise reduction accompanied by a shift toward lower-frequency noise texture. Conclusions PIQE and TrueFidelity demonstrated distinct dose-dependent image quality behavior. PIQE provided substantial noise reduction and high task-based spatial resolution at higher dose levels, consistent with its 1024 matrix super-resolution implementation, but showed stronger dose dependence in TTF, NMR, and CFR. TrueFidelity demonstrated more stable spatial resolution and noise texture across dose levels, with more modest noise reduction. Although newer DLR algorithms demonstrate substantial potential for noise reduction, their effects on spatial resolution, noise magnitude, and noise texture must be characterized before aggressive dose reductions are implemented.

title: Automatic Lesion Morphometrics Reliably Predict Sensorimotor Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury: A Longitudinal, Multicenter Neuroimaging Study.
abstract: Objective To evaluate automatic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived lesion morphometrics against manual measurements and their prognostic value for characterizing distinct acute to chronic neurological recovery trajectories after spinal cord injury (SCI). Methods We studied a retrospective, multicenter cohort of cervical and thoracolumbar SCI patients who underwent routine clinical MRI at 3-4 weeks post-SCI and neurological examinations over 6 months. Lesion severity was quantified using both established manual measurements and a novel automatic approach. We assessed the between-method agreement of MRI-derived lesion morphometrics, including lesion length, lesion width, and tissue bridge width, and their ability to stratify patients according to 6-month motor and sensory outcomes. Data-driven prediction models were used to identify clinically meaningful lesion measures and their respective thresholds, differentiating subgroups of specific recovery profiles. Results Eighty-three patients from eight sites were included. Automatically derived lesion morphometrics showed moderate to strong agreement with established manual measures (Spearman's ρ: 0.540-0.821, p < 0.001), capturing inter-individual differences in lesion severity and demonstrating comparable prognostic value. Lesion width represented the strongest predictor of 6-month neurological outcomes, splitting patients into recovery-specific subgroups. Patients with a smaller lesion width (threshold: 5.88-6.41 mm) demonstrated higher 6-month sensorimotor scores and superior recovery trajectories, while tissue bridges (threshold: 0.17 mm) further refined motor prediction-based stratification of more severely affected patients. Interpretation Automatic MRI measures of lesion severity hold promise as scalable, time-efficient in vivo biomarkers of SCI prognosis, with potential for clinical adoption to guide treatment decisions and multicenter trial planning.

title: CrystaL Artificial Intelligence Monitoring (CLAIM) Study of the OMERACT Ultrasound CPPD Subtask Working Group: Interim Analysis of Automated Ultrasound Grading of Knee Meniscal CPPD.
abstract: Objective We aimed to develop and evaluate artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods for automated grading of calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) in ultrasound (US) images according to the Outcome Measures in Rheumatology (OMERACT) US scoring system. Methods Within the OMERACT CrystaL Artificial Intelligence Monitoring (CLAIM) project, two deep learning strategies were explored using knee meniscus US images graded from 0 to 3. Image-level classification was evaluated using convolutional neural networks (CNN) trained directly on cropped meniscus images (n = 446). A semantic segmentation approach was developed using a subset of 279 images with manually annotated masks identifying meniscus and deposits. Models were evaluated using an 80/20 training-validation split and stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Segmentation was assessed using Intersection over Union (IoU). For automated grading, an area ratio (AR), representing CPPD pixels relative to meniscus and CPPD pixels, was applied to predicted masks. Objective

We aimed to develop and evaluate artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods for automated grading of calcium pyrophosphate deposition (CPPD) in ultrasound (US) images according to the Outcome Measures in Rheumatology (OMERACT) US scoring system.

Methods

Within the OMERACT CrystaL Artificial Intelligence Monitoring (CLAIM) project, two deep learning strategies were explored using knee meniscus US images graded from 0 to 3. Image-level classification was evaluated using convolutional neural networks (CNN) trained directly on cropped meniscus images (n = 446). A semantic segmentation approach was developed using a subset of 279 images with manually annotated masks identifying meniscus and deposits. Models were evaluated using an 80/20 training-validation split and stratified 5-fold cross-validation. Segmentation was assessed using Intersection over Union (IoU). For automated grading, an area ratio (AR), representing CPPD pixels relative to meniscus and CPPD pixels, was applied to predicted masks.

Results

Image-level classification achieved an accuracy of 0.69 in the single-split analysis and a mean accuracy of 0.59 (SD 0.10) in 5-fold cross-validation. End-to-end AR grading achieved accuracies of 0.64 and 0.61 (SD 0.10), with a grade 3 recall of 0.25 in the single split. AR grading on manually annotated reference masks achieved an accuracy of 0.82. The best-performing segmentation model achieved mean IoUs of 0.86 for background, 0.60 for meniscus, and 0.37 for CPPD.

Conclusions

These findings provide a methodological basis for automated CPPD US grading, but performance remains far from clinical applicability, highlighting the need for larger datasets and improved segmentation.

title: Biomarker Associations Between KL-6, CCL18, SP-D and Progressive or Severe SSc-ILD: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a multiorgan rheumatologic disease in which interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a prominent, often debilitating manifestation. Noninvasive serum biomarkers - Krebs von den Lungen-6 (KL-6), C-C motif chemokine ligand 18 (CCL18), and surfactant protein-D (SP-D) - have been proposed as prognostic markers in SSc-ILD. This study aimed to determine the association between serum KL-6, CCL18, and SP-D levels and severe and/or progressive SSc-ILD. Methods This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-concordant systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane for studies evaluating serum biomarker levels in SSc-ILD patients. The primary analysis was a correlation meta-analysis of biomarkers with pulmonary function parameters - forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLco) - followed by univariate meta-regression. Secondary analyses included a regression meta-analysis of biomarker elevation and odds ratio (OR) of progressive or severe disease, a mean difference meta-analysis, and a sensitivity/specificity meta-analysis. Results Forty-four studies were included. KL-6 negatively correlated with FVC% (r = -0.414) and DLco% (r = -0.402), and positively with high-resolution computed tomography percent (HRCT%; r = 0.611). SP-D negatively correlated with FVC% (r = -0.282) and DLco% (r = -0.347), and positively with HRCT% (r = 0.351). CCL18 showed weaker correlations. Change in KL-6 strongly correlated with change in FVC% (r = -0.754) and predicted progressive disease (OR = 2.83). High baseline KL-6 predicted severe (OR = 7.86) and progressive (OR = 1.87) disease; high CCL18 predicted severe disease (OR = 4.02). Both KL-6 and SP-D were elevated in progressive and severe ILD. Conclusion Serum KL-6, SP-D, and CCL18 are significantly associated with SSc-ILD activity and may aid noninvasive risk stratification, though standardized thresholds remain needed.

title: Microwave-Responsive AIE Nanocomposite Induces Immunogenic Senescence for Imaging-Guided Therapy and Bone Repair in Osteosarcoma.
abstract: Osteosarcoma remains challenging due to incomplete tumor resection, local recurrence, and limited immunostimulatory efficacy of current microwave (MW)-based therapies. Here, we develop a multifunctional theranostic nanoplatform, GPC3@TTBC, by conjugating an osteosarcoma-targeting anti-GPC3 peptide onto aggregation-induced emission (AIE) nanoparticles. GPC3@TTBC enables selective tumor accumulation and high-contrast near-infrared fluorescence imaging, allowing precise tumor margin delineation and superior tumor-to-background resolution compared with clinically used dyes, including effective visualization in patient-derived xenograft models. Upon MW irradiation, lysosome-localized GPC3@TTBC generates robust nonthermal reactive oxygen species (ROS) through enhanced charge separation and electron transfer, resulting in substantial tumor cell apoptosis while simultaneously inducing a prominent immunogenic senescence-associated phenotype and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) response. Importantly, MW + GPC3@TTBC suppressed tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and reduced pulmonary metastatic lesions in vivo. Meanwhile, the SASP promoted dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte activation, thereby enhancing antitumor immune responses and remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment. Beyond tumor eradication, GPC3@TTBC facilitates osteogenic microenvironment reconstruction and bone regeneration after tumor clearance, while exhibiting favorable biosafety. Collectively, GPC3@TTBC integrates targeted fluorescence-guided imaging, MW-enhanced ROS generation, immunogenic senescence induction, and bone regeneration, providing a comprehensive theranostic strategy for precise osteosarcoma treatment.

title: Molecular MRI Reveals Macrophage-Enriched Peritumoral Immune Remodeling After Incomplete Ablation in Liver Cancer.
abstract: Incomplete image-guided ablation can promote local tumor progression by reshaping the residual tumor microenvironment toward immunosuppression, yet noninvasive biomarkers of this process remain limited. Here, a translational multiparametric PET/MRI strategy was developed to monitor macrophage-associated microenvironmental remodeling after incomplete microwave ablation (iMWA) in orthotopic VX2 liver tumors. Twenty-four tumor-bearing rabbits were assigned to untreated control, early post-iMWA (short-term), or late post-iMWA (long-term) groups and underwent clinical 3 T PET/MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, [ 1 8 F]FDG PET, and T2-weighted MRI before and after administration of Eu-VSOP. Eu-VSOP-enhanced MRI revealed a hypointense peritumoral rim after iMWA, with the largest rim-to-liver signal decrease and rim thickness observed in the long-term group. Prussian blue staining and LA-ICP-ToF-MS demonstrated preferential iron and europium enrichment in macrophage-rich, CD206-associated peritumoral regions. Histology and proteomics further demonstrated increased CD206 and MMP-9 expression, extracellular matrix remodeling, immunosuppressive myeloid-associated changes, and metabolic reprogramming in viable residual tumors, accompanied by altered [ 1 8 F]FDG uptake. Together, these findings indicate that incomplete ablation induces a temporally evolving, macrophage-rich immunosuppressive peritumoral niche and support the potential of Eu-VSOP-enhanced multiparametric PET/MRI for noninvasive monitoring of post-ablation microenvironmental remodeling.

title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction.
abstract: The rise of Alzheimer's disease (AD) immunotherapies underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. MRI-based deep learning shows promise in this regard, yet few models have undergone comprehensive clinical validation. Using the SILCODE cohort (722 Chinese participants, 1,105 scans), we test the transportability of our classifier (pretrained on Western samples) to an independent Chinese cohort without retraining. The associations between risk scores and disease progression, cognitive performance, and plasma biomarkers are examined. In addition, an interpretable framework is developed to generate individualized brain risk maps and identify subtypes. The model classifies AD with an AUC of 0.913 and 95.2% sensitivity, identifying 90.5% of high-risk individuals 2-3 years before clinical diagnosis. Risk scores correlate significantly with cognitive and plasma indices, particularly p-tau 217. Brain risk maps reveal AD subtypes, including a subgroup with rapid cognitive decline. These findings establish a population-robust, clinically relevant MRI-based model for early AD detection and risk stratification.

title: A CT Lesion Foundation Model for Non-Invasive Assessment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Aggressiveness and Prediction of Recurrence Risk.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with high recurrence rates following curative resection. Accurate non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and recurrence risk is critical for surgical decision-making and postoperative surveillance, yet remains challenging with conventional imaging modalities. Here, we developed a CT lesion foundation model (LFM), trained via self-supervised learning on 32,120 generic lesion and 6,387 HCC-specific CT patches to capture transferable intra-lesional imaging phenotypes. Across one internal and two external validation cohorts, the sequentially pretrained LFM (LFM-Seq) achieved area under the curve values of 0.916, 0.846, and 0.920 for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment, and 0.833, 0.885 and 0.795 for pathological grade assessment. The model remained robust under scenarios of limited training data and tumor localization perturbations. Furthermore, LFM-Seq-derived risk scores stratified recurrence-free survival (RFS), yielding an externally validated C-index of 0.701, and remained independently associated with RFS after adjusting for clinicopathological factors. Exploratory biological interpretability analyses showed that LFM-Seq-derived risk phenotypes were associated with suppressed lymphocyte-related immune programs. These results suggest that CT lesion foundation models can support non-invasive and robust characterization of HCC aggressiveness, recurrence risk stratification and discovery of interpretable prognostic imaging biomarkers.

title: 18 F-FGln PET/CT Imaging of Glutamine Uptake Has Potential for Predicting Immunotherapy Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: We investigated whether glutamine (Gln) uptake, imaged by 18 F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine ( 18 F-FGln) PET/CT, could predict and modulate immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (LIHC) dataset revealed that SLC1A5 expression-which encodes a primary Gln uptake channel in HCC cells-was significantly associated with poor prognosis, higher tumor grade, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In murine HCC models, tumors with high 18 F-FGln uptake exhibited elevated Slc1a5 expression and poor response to anti-PD-1 therapy, whereas low-uptake tumors were more sensitive to immunotherapy. Genetic knockdown of Slc1a5 reduced 18 F-FGln uptake, enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy, increased cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, and decreased regulatory T cell abundance. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed activation of antitumor immune pathways and reprogramming toward an immune-inflamed phenotype after Slc1a5 suppression. V-9302 decreased tumor Gln uptake, as measured by 18 F-FGln PET/CT, and sensitized HCC to PD-1 blockade. In patient-derived organoid-T cell co-culture systems, low-SLC1A5 organoids were susceptible to PD-1 blockade, whereas high-SLC1A5 organoids were resistant, consistent with 18 F-FGln PET/CT findings. These results identify Gln uptake as a checkpoint of immune evasion in HCC and support that 18 F-FGln PET/CT has the potential to predict and monitor immunotherapy response.

title: Deep Learning Model Based on Automated CT Image Segmentation for Predicting Pathological Complete Response in Lung Cancer Patients Receiving Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy and Chemotherapy: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: Background This study aims to establish a deep learning model based on interactive 3D segmentation to predict NICT efficacy. Methods This study collected 517 NSCLC patients who underwent NICT and surgery at three centers. VISTA3D is applied in this study for CT images to achieve automatic tumor identification in NSCLC patients via automated segmentation combined with point prompts. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to compare the tumor immune microenvironment between low-risk and high-risk patients stratified by the model. Based on this model, patients likely to benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy are identified. Results This model attained AUC values of 0.83 and 0.81 for cohort A and C, with a Dice coefficient reaching 0.83 ± 0.14. Patients identified as high-risk by the model showed a potential survival advantage with adjuvant immunotherapy (HR: 0.55 for DFS; HR: 0.51 for OS). Exploratory multiplex immunofluorescence analysis suggested compositional differences in the tumor immune microenvironment between risk groups. Conclusion The deep learning model developed in this study, based on interactive segmentation, achieves comparable performance to manual segmentation and assists clinicians in effectively predicting pCR in NSCLC patients undergoing NICT prior to surgical treatment. Furthermore, adjuvant immunotherapy was associated with improved survival in high-risk patients, requiring prospective validation.

title: Prenatal Detection of Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita, Present State and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC) is a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by congenital contractures in at least two different body regions. Despite increasingly widespread prenatal ultrasound screening, prenatal detection rates for AMC remain disappointingly low, with fewer than half of affected fetuses diagnosed before birth. Missed or late diagnosis limits opportunities for informed counseling, optimal delivery planning, and early postnatal intervention. In this overview, we summarize current knowledge on prenatal detection of AMC, drawing on international cohort studies, registry data, literature on fetal motor assessment, and patient-reported experiences. We highlight the added value of systematic evaluation of fetal movements in addition to repeated structural anomaly scans, the role of multidisciplinary care pathways, and the importance of phenotypic classification (AMC Groups 1-3) for prognosis and counseling. We also review current and emerging genetic testing strategies, including exome- and genome-based approaches, and their diagnostic yield in fetuses with contractures. Finally, we outline future perspectives for international collaboration, standardized data collection from fetus to adulthood, and research priorities with patient support organizations. Together, these efforts aim to improve awareness, earlier recognition, and more tailored counseling for parents confronted with contractures and the possibility of diagnosing AMC during their pregnancies.

title: The Prenatal Phenotype: Illustrating the Complexities of Genetic Testing and Interpretation With the Goal of Understanding the Fetal Presentation of Genetic Disease.
abstract: Advanced prenatal imaging and chromosomal microarray have improved detection of fetal anomalies, yet many structurally abnormal fetuses remain without a unifying diagnosis. This manuscript describes representative prenatal cases evaluated with genome sequencing (GS) or exome sequencing (ES), demonstrating how genomic data refine etiologic understanding, reshape counseling, and reveal the complexities of variant interpretation within the prenatal context. Three illustrative fetal cases were selected based on characteristic imaging findings, including short long bones, echogenic kidneys, multisystem anomalies, and severe limb reduction defects. All underwent detailed ultrasound, standard genetic evaluation, and ultimately GS or ES. Variants were classified using ACMG/AMP criteria with prenatal-specific interpretive considerations. Diagnoses included a 17q12 deletion with concomitant ARID1B-related Coffin-Siris syndrome, a de novo FRYL variant in the setting of multisystem anomalies, and a de novo KMT2E truncating variant identified alongside placental pathology supportive of treated leptospirosis. Findings alter recurrence risks, reveal dual diagnoses, and highlight prognostic complexities. Prenatal sequencing clarifies fetal diagnoses, informs reproductive planning, and refines risk counseling, yet interpretation is constrained by limited prenatal phenotyping and reliance on postnatal genotype-phenotype literature. Integration of GS/ES with imaging and multidisciplinary counseling is essential as sequencing becomes routine in perinatal care.

title: Development and External Validation of a Machine Learning-Based Predictive Model for Postoperative Recurrence in Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis.
abstract: Background Pediatric chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) frequently recurs after endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS), but reliable preoperative predictors are lacking, and adult-derived models may not apply to children. We developed and externally validated machine learning (ML) models to predict postoperative recurrence in pediatric CRS and identified key prognostic factors. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, ML models-logistic regression (LR), random forest, XGBoost, and a stacking ensemble-were trained with class weighting on a development cohort of 633 pediatric ESS patients (aged 0-18 years), and an L1-optimized LR model was developed for variable selection from 33 candidate predictors. Performance was estimated by fivefold cross-validation, and the model was externally validated in 152 independent patients. Calibration was assessed using the Brier score, intercept, slope, and Hosmer-Lemeshow test, with logistic recalibration. Results Recurrence occurred in 242 of 633 patients (38.2%) in the development cohort and 46 of 152 patients (30.3%) in the external validation cohort. The L1-optimized LR model retained three predictors-nasal polyps, a higher Lund-Mackay CT score, and diffuse extent-each associated with higher recurrence risk, and achieved an AUC of 0.689, comparable to that of the other four class-weighted models. Laboratory findings and clinical symptoms were less predictive. On external validation, the model maintained discrimination (AUC = 0.756) but showed systematic miscalibration. Logistic recalibration restored calibration with essentially unchanged discrimination. Conclusions The three-variable L1-optimized LR model provides a concise framework for preoperative recurrence risk stratification in pediatric CRS that could inform postoperative surveillance. A site-specific recalibration step is required before application to populations with different recurrence rates.

title: Optimized amyloid-β PET centiloid and cognitive cutoffs predict progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's dementia.
abstract: Introduction This study aimed to develop optimized prognostic cutoffs for amyloid-β-positron emission tomography (Aβ-PET) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) that predict 3-year progression from Clinical Dementia Rating Global (CDR-Global) score 0.5 to 1.0 in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) participants and validate against cognitive decline/functional trajectories. Methods We analyzed 454 CDR-global = 0.5 Aβ-positive (> 25 Centiloid [CL]) MCI participants from Australian Imaging Biomarkers and Lifestyle (AIBL) (N = 99) and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) (N = 355), followed up to seven years. Youden index derived optimal Aβ-PET and MMSE thresholds for 3-year progression. Participants were stratified into four groups by combined Aβ-PET/MMSE status. Adjusted Cox models (age, sex, education, apolipoprotein E [APOE] ε4) assessed progression to CDR-Global score of 1.0 Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia (confirmed with Aβ-PET); adjusted linear mixed models assessed CDR Sum of Boxes (CDR-SoB) and Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite (PACC) trajectories. Results Optimal cutoffs were Aβ-PET > 71 CL (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.67; 3-year risk = 36.7%) and MMSE score of < 27 (HR = 2.27; 36.8%). The combined high Aβ/low MMSE group showed a 6.39-fold risk and 47.8% 3-year progression, with the steepest decline. Discussion Prognostically optimized Aβ-PET and MMSE cutoffs improve 3-year risk stratification beyond common diagnostic thresholds, supporting dual-cutoff prognostic enrichment.

Optimal cutoffs were Aβ-PET > 71 CL (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.67; 3-year risk = 36.7%) and MMSE score of < 27 (HR = 2.27; 36.8%). The combined high Aβ/low MMSE group showed a 6.39-fold risk and 47.8% 3-year progression, with the steepest decline.

Discussion

Prognostically optimized Aβ-PET and MMSE cutoffs improve 3-year risk stratification beyond common diagnostic thresholds, supporting dual-cutoff prognostic enrichment.

title: AI-Integrated multimodal neuroimaging in Alzheimer's disease: toward biologically informed precision diagnostics.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), which is characterized by the progressive accumulation of amyloid beta plaques and neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), metabolic dysfunction, and neuroinflammation, is the most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder. The distinct pathological features of AD can be characterized in vivo via neuroimaging: Structural magnetic resonance imaging captures brain atrophy, while positron emission tomography detects Aβ/NFT deposition. The application of artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the interpretation of neuroimaging data, but single-modality AI provides only limited biological information. This limitation has motivated the development of multimodal approaches that integrate complementary imaging, molecular, and clinical data for diagnosis and prognosis. However, there has been no comprehensive examination of how modality-specific neuroimaging information is incorporated into single-modality AI and subsequently integrated within multimodal frameworks. This review addresses this gap by evaluating conventional neuroimaging, single-modality AI, and multimodal AI as part of a unified framework, with particular emphasis on the added diagnostic and prognostic value of multimodal integration. We further identify key methodological and translational bottlenecks in developing clinically robust multimodal AI, including cross-modal and cross-cohort heterogeneity, model complexity, missing modalities, interpretability, and generalizability. Finally, we propose a translational roadmap emphasizing data harmonization, independent external validation, clinically meaningful explainability, and prospective evaluation. Ultimately, the clinical value of multimodal AI will depend on whether its added predictive value is reproducible across independent populations and translates into meaningful improvements in clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.

title: Accelerated clinical evaluations for Alzheimer's disease: feasibility across specialty and rural care settings.
abstract: Introduction Timely diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly important given the availability of disease-modifying therapies, yet current diagnostic pathways remain fragmented, resource-intensive, and difficult to access. We developed the accelerated clinical evaluation for Alzheimer's disease (ACE-AD), a nursing-led workflow integrating a clinical interview, cognitive testing, blood biomarkers, and portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to streamline dementia evaluation. Methods ACE-AD was evaluated in two phases. Phase 1 validated the workflow in 20 participants with standard-of-care (SOC) memory clinic diagnoses compared against ACE-AD-derived etiologic diagnosis, cognitive staging, and neuroimaging findings. Phase 2 adapted the workflow for a rural neurology practice, assessing feasibility, utility, and acceptability. Results In Phase 1 (n = 20), primary etiologic diagnoses were universally concordant between SOC and ACE-AD evaluations, with 90% agreement on AD as a primary or contributing etiology. Cognitive stage agreed in 13 participants (65%); ACE-AD rated all discordant cases as less impaired. Portable MRI identified clinically relevant abnormalities consistent with SOC MRI, and patients, care partners, and clinicians rated the workflow highly acceptable. In Phase 2 (n = 7), the rural neurologist reported improved diagnostic confidence, efficiency, treatment planning, and patient communication without workflow disruption. Discussion A structured, nursing-led evaluation integrating blood biomarkers and portable MRI can capture sufficient clinical information to support specialist dementia diagnosis while shifting much of the diagnostic workup earlier in the care pathway. These findings support further evaluation of ACE-AD as a scalable approach for expanding access to timely dementia diagnosis in both specialty and resource-limited settings.

A structured, nursing-led evaluation integrating blood biomarkers and portable MRI can capture sufficient clinical information to support specialist dementia diagnosis while shifting much of the diagnostic workup earlier in the care pathway. title: Prognostic value of plasma brain-derived phosphorylated Tau.
abstract: Introduction Plasma brain-derived phosphorylated Tau217 (BD-pTau217) may provide a more Alzheimer's disease (AD) -specific plasma tau measure than total pTau217, but its prognostic value is unclear. Methods We compared baseline plasma NULISAseq biomarkers for amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) progression (positivity: Centiloid ≥ 24.1; n = 175) and clinical progression to mild cognitive impairment or AD dementia (n = 508) in cognitively unimpaired Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) participants using Cox models and time-dependent areas under the curve (tdAUCs). Results Over a median clinical follow-up of 6 years (interquartile range [IQR], 3.0-7.3), BD-pTau217 and total pTau217 had similar discrimination (full-follow-up AUC = 0.66 each; high-versus-low hazard ratios [HRs]; 95% confidence interval [CIs]: 2.8 [1.89-4.06] and 2.9 [1.96-4.35], respectively). Among initially amyloid-negative participants, BD-pTau217 better predicted progression to amyloid PET positivity at 2.5 years (tdAUC 0.82 vs. 0.69; HR = 10.54 [95% CI 2.3-48.1], p = 0.00015) and 4 years (tdAUC 0.77 vs. 0.64; HR = 7.03 [95% CI 1.9-25.6], p = 0.00055) compared to total pTau217. Conclusion BD-pTau217 better predicted near-term progression to amyloid PET positivity than total pTau217, but showed no advantage for clinical progression, supporting its potential value as an early marker of AD pathological change.

title: Anatomical and histological characterization of the heart of the scarlet ibis (Eudocimus ruber).
abstract: Detailed information on the cardiac morphology of the scarlet ibis (Eudocimus ruber) remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the gross and microscopic anatomy of this species' heart and provide morphometric data. We examined six specimens (three males and three females) using gross anatomical analysis, morphometry, conventional radiography, three-dimensional scanning, light microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy. The mean heart mass was 5.93 ± 1.49 g (n = 6), corresponding to 1.10 ± 0.23% of body mass, and the mean radiographic cardiothoracic ratio was 66.90 ± 5.78% (n = 3). Macroscopic examination identified three venae cavae: the right and left cranial venae cavae and the caudal vena cava. The left atrioventricular valve had two cusps with chordae tendineae and papillary muscles, whereas the right atrioventricular valve had a single muscular fold. Histological examination identified uninucleated and binucleated Purkinje fibers in the subendocardial region, extending into myocardial muscle bundles. The base of the aorta showed hyaline cartilage containing chondrocytes and chondroblasts, with no bone tissue identified in the examined sections. These findings provide anatomical, morphometric, and histological data on the heart of E. ruber and a basis for future comparative studies of avian cardiac morphology.

title: A comprehensive review of craniomandibular morphometric indices in carnivora: Anatomical basis, functional significance, and comparative applications.
abstract: The skull of carnivorans represents a highly integrated anatomical structure shaped by selective pressures associated with feeding ecology, sensory specialization, locomotion, and phylogenetic history. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of craniomandibular morphometric indices in the order Carnivora, integrating their anatomical definitions, morphometric foundations, and functional significance. Standardized cranial and mandibular measurements are reviewed together with 11 widely used proportional indices, including the Cranial Index (CI), Skull Index (SI), Facial Index (FI), Facial Length Index (FLI), Cranial Length Index (CLI), Cranial Height Index (CHI), Orbital Index (OI), Palatal Index (PI), Foramen Magnum Index (FMI), Mandibular Body Index (MBI), and Mandibular Ramus Index (MRI). The review highlights the biomechanical and evolutionary relevance of these indices by examining their relationships with bite performance, craniofacial organization, sensory adaptations, feeding ecology, and morphological diversification among carnivoran families. In addition to summarizing published morphometric indices, several proportional indices that have rarely been reported as independent variables are derived from previously published linear craniometric measurements, providing standardized quantitative descriptors for comparative analyses across species. By compiling anatomical landmarks, measurement protocols, functional interpretations, and comparative data within a unified framework, this review identifies current knowledge gaps and promotes greater methodological consistency in future studies. Although some proportional indices were calculated from published measurements rather than directly reported in the original literature, they provide valuable complementary metrics for evaluating cranial and mandibular morphology. Overall, the integration of these 11 morphometric indices offers a comprehensive approach for investigating craniofacial evolution, functional morphology, feeding adaptations, and taxonomic diversity in both extant and fossil carnivorans. This review provides a practical reference for researchers in comparative anatomy, evolutionary biology, paleontology, and veterinary morphology.

title: Indole as a Privileged Scaffold in Anti-Leukaemic Drug Discovery: Synthetic Approaches and Biological Insights.
abstract: The indole scaffold is a backbone in medicinal chemistry and is versatile as a privileged pharmacophore in anticancer drug discovery. The indole scaffold interacts with various biological targets, including protein kinases and nucleic acids such as DNA. Its planar aromatic structure and hydrogen-bonding properties may contribute to these interactions. Despite the clinical success of certain indole-based drugs, the development of effective targeted treatment for leukaemia remains challenging, highlighting the need for novel chemotypes. This review provides advances in the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of indole-based antileukaemic derivatives, particularly against HL-60 cells. It highlights the synthetic routes to structural modifications of the indole core, oxindole and isatin derivatives, indole hybrid pharmacophores, and fused polycyclic systems, including catalyst- and coupling-mediated routes and green approaches (ultrasound-mediated synthesis). The structural modifications involve substitution at the specific N-1, C-2 and C-3 positions of the indole core and on the fused benzo ring, with electron-donating groups, electron-withdrawing groups, and heterocyclic linkers that modulate lipophilicity, electronic character, and target-binding affinity. The indole derivatives were the most potent family, and the highest activity was found with substitution at two or more positions of the pyrrole ring. N-1 and C-2 substitution gave compound 16c (GI 50 = 0.103 µM), and substitution at C-2 and C-3 gave compound 25b (IC 50 = 0.53 µM). Monosubstituted indoles were less active (IC 50 1.3-23.9 µM), and oxindoles and isatin were active in the low-micromolar range. Future perspectives focus on the design of more selective and effective indole-based antileukaemic drugs.

title: Inferior Patient-Reported Outcomes After Primary Hip Arthroscopy in the Congenitally Narrow Joint Despite Similar Cartilage Quality When Compared With a Propensity-Matched Control Group.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the outcomes after hip arthroscopy in patients with a symmetric congenitally narrowed hip joint space without radiographic evidence of degenerative changes. Methods Consecutive patients with Tönnis grade 0 undergoing hip arthroscopy between 2009 and 2022 for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome with labral repair and minimum 2-year postoperative outcomes were eligible for inclusion in the study. Subjects were considered congenitally narrowed if they had an average bilateral joint space width less than 3 mm without other radiographic evidence of osteoarthritis. This cohort was propensity-matched to patients with an average joint space greater than 4 mm. Preoperative demographic and radiographic variables, intraoperative findings and procedures, and postoperative outcomes were compared between the 2 groups. Results Thirty-one patients in the congenitally narrow group were propensity-matched to 57 patients in the control cohort. The groups were comparable in age, gender, body mass index, and radiographic variables other than joint space width between cohorts. The congenitally narrow group had no differences in femoral head or acetabular chondral damage compared with the control cohort (P > .05 for both). There were significantly lower postoperative patient-reported outcomes in the congenitally narrow group across multiple patient reported outcome measures. At 5-year time point, the control group had a significantly higher percentage, meeting patient acceptable symptomatic state for modified Harris Hip Score (80% vs 52%, P = .01) and International Hip Outcome Tool-12 (80% vs 56%, P = .03) and minimal clinically important difference for modified Harris Hip Score (89.5% vs 63%). There was no difference in revision arthroscopy (9.7% vs 10.5%, P = .9) or arthroplasty-free survivorship (100% vs 96.5%; P = .29) between the congenitally narrow and control groups, respectively. Conclusions There were no differences in intraoperative cartilage quality or reoperation rate in patients with a congenitally narrow joint compared with a propensity-matched control cohort. However, despite the lack of radiographic osteoarthritis, patients with a congenitally narrow joint had inferior patient-reported outcomes scores compared with the study control group. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective cohort study.

At 5-year time point, the control group had a significantly higher percentage, meeting patient acceptable symptomatic state for modified Harris Hip Score (80% vs 52%, P = .01) and International Hip Outcome Tool-12 (80% vs 56%, P = .03) and minimal clinically important difference for modified Harris Hip Score (89.5% vs 63%). There was no difference in revision arthroscopy (9.7% vs 10.5%, P = .9) or arthroplasty-free survivorship (100% vs 96.5%; P = .29) between the congenitally narrow and control groups, respectively.

Conclusions

There were no differences in intraoperative cartilage quality or reoperation rate in patients with a congenitally narrow joint compared with a propensity-matched control cohort. However, despite the lack of radiographic osteoarthritis, patients with a congenitally narrow joint had inferior patient-reported outcomes scores compared with the study control group.

title: Anatomical Risk Factors for Patellofemoral Instability Vary by Dejour Type of Trochlear Dysplasia.
abstract: Purpose To assess whether Dejour trochlear dysplasia (TD) types differ in their association with other patellofemoral anatomical variables in patients with patellar instability. Methods All patients with TD undergoing evaluation for patellar instability between January 2010 and December 2020 were included if a true lateral radiograph and a preoperative magnetic resonance imaging were available. Two reviewers independently assessed TD type (Dejour classification), femorotibial rotation, tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TTTG) distance, sagittal TTTG, tibial tubercle-to-posterior cruciate ligament distance, supratrochlear spur height, sulcus depth, Merchant's congruence angle, trochlear sulcus angle, Caton-Deschamps index, patellotrochlear index, patellar tilt, angle, thickness, and width. Results The study included 330 patients (363 knees, 66.7% women, mean age 22.5 ± 7.9 years, body mass index 24.9 ± 5.4). TD distribution was type A (17.1%), B (33.6%), C (25.9%), and D (23.4%). Types B and D showed significantly increased Merchant's congruence angle ( P = .019), patellar tilt ( P < .001), patellotrochlear index ( P = .035), TTTG ( P < .001), sagittal TTTG ( P < .001), and femorotibial rotation ( P < .001). Conclusions Patients with Dejour type B and D TD had significantly increased values in other patellofemoral instability risk factors compared with those presenting with type A and C dysplasia. Level of evidence Level IV, diagnostic retrospective case series.

title: Connecting Ligament Tears of the Lateral Meniscus in the Popliteal Hiatus Region: An Arthroscopic Classification Including 4 Types.
abstract: Purpose To describe an arthroscopic classification system for connecting ligament tears in the popliteal hiatus of the lateral meniscus and describe their repair technique. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the data of patients who underwent lateral meniscus repair between 2019 and 2023. Inclusion criteria included isolated or combined tears of the connecting ligaments in the popliteal hiatus. All patients underwent arthroscopic examination and/or repair and were followed up for a minimum of 1 year. Tears were classified arthroscopically into 4 types: type 1, isolated radial tear of the meniscofibular ligament; type 2, isolated longitudinal tear of the meniscofibular ligament; type 3, isolated longitudinal tear of the posterior popliteomeniscal fascicle; and type 4, combined longitudinal tear of meniscofibular ligament and posterior popliteomeniscal fascicle. Clinical outcomes were assessed using Lysholm, Tegner, and International Knee Documentation Committee scores. Knee magnetic resonance imaging was performed at 1 year postoperatively. Results Among 188 patients with lateral meniscus tears, 24 (12.8%) had connecting ligament tears in the popliteal hiatus. These included 3 type 1 (12.5%), 4 type 2 (16.7%), 8 type 3 (33.3%), and 9 type 4 (37.5%) lesions. Mean postoperative Lysholm, Tegner, and International Knee Documentation Committee scores significantly improved compared with preoperative values (all P < .01). Magnetic resonance imaging at 1-year follow-up showed evidence of ligament healing in 15 of 21 evaluated patients (71.4%). Conclusions This study describes an arthroscopic classification of popliteal hiatus-lateral meniscus tears. Additionally, all-inside suture arthroscopic repair of the popliteal hiatus ligament-lateral meniscus complex led to favorable patient-reported outcomes at short-term follow-up. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective therapeutic case series.

title: Open-Source and Commercial 3-Dimensional Computed Tomography Methods Show Limited Agreement for Classifying Acetabular Morphology in Patients Undergoing Hip Arthroscopy.
abstract: Purpose To compare acetabular morphology classifications derived from a validated open-source (freely available) method with those derived from commercially available software in patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome. Methods We analyzed preoperative 3-dimensional computed tomography imaging in patients with femoroacetabular impingement syndrome using open-source and commercial software. The open-source method calculated acetabular coverage across 5 regions and generated z -scores relative to an internal normative database. Hips with z -scores ≥2 or ≤-2 were classified as abnormal. The commercial method categorized hips as normal, undercovered, or overcovered based on published thresholds (lateral center-edge angle, Tönnis angle, coverage percentage, and crossover sign) and focal depth mapping. The primary outcome was categorical agreement between methods. Results Seventy-six hips (55 women, 21 men; mean age 35.5 ± 12.3 years) were included. The open-source method classified 58/76 hips as normal, 10/76 as dysplastic, and 8/76 as overcovered. The commercial method classified 14/76 hips as normal, 29/76 as undercovered, and 33/76 as overcovered. A total of 23/76 hips were classified the same in both systems and called agreed. Disagreements (53/76 hips) fell into 3 categories: (1) essentially similar despite different labels because of borderline z -scores or small focal areas (n = 24), (2) disagreements driven by Tönnis angle alone (n = 8), and (3) true disagreements (n = 21). Notably, 5 hips (6.6%) showed opposite classifications (e.g., dysplastic vs overcovered). Subanalysis of z -scores showed that 69.8% of disagreements reflected borderline morphology ( z -scores of ±1-2). Conclusions Although both open-source and commercial methods provide 3-dimensional classification of acetabular morphology, categorical agreement was limited. Most disagreements reflected borderline morphology or small focal areas of uncertain clinical relevance. A minority showed true classification opposites. Clinical relevance Awareness of the methodological differences between open-source and commercial 3-dimensional computed tomography platforms may help surgeons appropriately interpret acetabular morphology classifications during preoperative planning for patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Percutaneous Achilles Repair Improves Suture Placement Accuracy and Reduces the Rate of Conversion to Open Repair.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether intraoperative ultrasound (US) guidance during percutaneous Achilles tendon repair using the Percutaneous Achilles Repair System (PARS) improves suture placement accuracy and reduces the rate of intraoperative conversion to open repair compared with repair performed without US. Methods A retrospective comparative study was performed on patients with acute or subacute Achilles tendon ruptures who underwent primary percutaneous repair using PARS by a single surgeon between June 2022 and November 2025 with a minimum of 6 months of postoperative follow-up. Patients were divided into 2 groups: PARS with US guidance (PARS US) and PARS without US (PARS no-US). Suture placement accuracy, intraoperative conversion to open repair, tourniquet times, and postoperative complications were recorded and compared between groups. Results Thirty-nine patients were included: 24 in the PARS US group and 15 in the PARS no-US group. The mean follow-up was 8.5 months (range: 6-12 months) in the PARS US group and 8.9 months (range: 6.4-11.5 months) in the PARS no-US group ( P = .541). Baseline demographics and time to surgery were comparable between groups. The PARS US group showed significantly higher suture placement accuracy compared with the PARS no-US group (98.2% [165/168] vs 76.2% [80/105], P = .005). Three patients (20%) in the PARS no-US group required intraoperative conversion to open repair because of inadequate suture purchase, whereas no conversions occurred in the PARS US group ( P = .049). Tourniquet times were significantly longer in cases requiring conversion to open repair compared with US-guided repairs ( P = .005). Overall tourniquet times were comparable between groups ( P = .324). Complication rates, including wound complications and rerupture, were low and comparable between groups. Conclusions In this single-surgeon retrospective series, US guidance during percutaneous Achilles tendon repair using the PARS system was associated with a significantly higher suture placement accuracy and a significantly lower rate of intraoperative conversion to open repair compared with repairs performed without US. The addition of US did not increase the overall tourniquet time or complication rates. Level of evidence Level III, retrospective comparative study.

title: Female Sex Is Independently Associated With Greater Sagittal Tibial Tubercle-Trochlear Groove Distance and Patellar Tilt in High-Grade Trochlear Dysplasia.
abstract: Purpose To assess sex-related differences in patellofemoral (PF) anatomy among patients with PF instability and high-grade trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types B-D). Methods Consecutive patients with symptomatic PF instability and high-grade trochlear dysplasia (Dejour types B-D) who were scheduled for surgical treatment between January 2010 and December 2020 and had available preoperative radiographs and magnetic resonance imaging were retrospectively identified at a single center. Patients with normal trochlear morphology, type A dysplasia, missing preoperative magnetic resonance imaging, or prior osseous procedures were excluded. Standardized magnetic resonance imaging-based measurements were obtained for trochlear morphology, tibial tubercle position, and patellar geometry. Depending on data distribution, parametric or nonparametric tests were used to compare sexes. Multivariate linear mixed-effects models were performed to calculate regression coefficients ( B ) with 95% confidence intervals, adjusting for patient clustering, age, body height, supratrochlear spur height, Caton-Deschamps index, sulcus depth, and tibiofemoral rotation. Results A total of 301 knees from 278 patients were analyzed; 192 knees (63.8%) were from female patients. The mean age was 22.6 ± 8.1 years (range, 11-50 years), and the mean body mass index was 24.9 ± 5.5 (range, 16.4-48.1). Distribution according to the Dejour classification was 40.5% type B, 31.2% type C, and 28.2% type D. Female patients showed smaller patellar width (37.9 ± 3.4 mm vs 41.3 ± 4.1 mm; P < .001) and thickness (16.8 ± 2.0 mm vs 18.5 ± 2.6 mm; P < .001), as well as greater patellar tilt (29.3° ± 10.7° vs 25.0° ± 10.8°; P = .001) and sagittal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (sTTTG) distance (9.9 ± 5.2 mm vs 8.4 ± 6.0 mm; P = .005). After adjustment for age and body height, differences in patellar width, patellar thickness, patellar tilt, and sTTTG remained significant. After additional adjustment for supratrochlear spur height, Caton-Deschamps index, sulcus depth, and tibiofemoral rotation, patellar tilt ( B = 3.51°, P = .021) and sTTTG distance ( B = 2.36 mm, P = .004) remained greater in female patients. Conclusions Among patients with PF instability and high-grade trochlear dysplasia, female sex was associated with greater patellar tilt and sTTTG distance after adjustment for age, body height, and relevant anatomical covariates. Level of evidence Level III, prognostic retrospective comparative study.

title: Pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty in adults: A technical refinement of Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty.
abstract: Objectives To describe pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty, a technical refinement of Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty for adult ureteropelvic junction obstruction, and to report perioperative and functional outcomes in an initial adult series. Methods Between 2009 and 2018, 12 adult patients with symptomatic ureteropelvic junction obstruction underwent pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty using a transperitoneal laparoscopic or robot-assisted approach. Preoperative evaluation included computed tomography intravenous pyelography and diuretic Tc-99m MAG3 renography. Patients with previous failed ureteropelvic junction surgery were excluded. The technique preserves and incorporates a sleeve of renal pelvic tissue into the reconstruction to create a broad, continuous, tension-free ureteropelvic anastomosis while minimizing manipulation of healthy ureteric tissue. Results All procedures were completed successfully without conversion to open surgery. Eight patients underwent laparoscopic and four underwent robot-assisted pyeloplasty. Mean operative time was 185 min (range 160-255 min), and estimated blood loss ranged from 90 to 350 mL. One patient had intraoperative bleeding from a gonadal vein injury, controlled without transfusion. One patient developed a transient postoperative febrile episode (Clavien-Dindo grade II). No patient developed urinary leakage or required secondary intervention. At a mean follow-up of 38 months (range 24-50 months), all patients were asymptomatic and diuretic Tc-99m MAG3 renography demonstrated unobstructed drainage. Conclusions Pelvic sleeve pyeloplasty is a feasible modification of dismembered pyeloplasty that preserves ureteric length, minimizes ureteric manipulation and facilitates a wide, continuous, tension-free ureteropelvic anastomosis. Larger comparative studies are required to validate reproducibility and long-term efficacy.

title: Targeting Ninjurin-1-Mediated Microglial Pyroptosis Attenuates Neuroinflammation and Neuronal Injury Following Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Objective This study aims to delineate the pathophysiological contribution of Ninjurin-1 (Ninj1) to secondary neural injury following intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), specifically elucidating its function in microglial pyroptosis and its upstream transcriptional governance by nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB). Methods Candidate targets were initially identified via in silico transcriptomic profiling. We subsequently employed a collagenase-induced murine ICH paradigm alongside hemin-challenged microglia. Mechanistic pathways were interrogated utilizing targeted genetic silencing (in vivo siRNA and in vitro shRNA) and pharmacological blockade. Disease phenotypes-encompassing pyroptotic execution, neuroinflammation, and collateral neuronal death-were quantified via immunoblotting, molecular assays, and histopathology. The upstream regulatory architecture was validated through ChIP-qPCR, EMSA, and dual-luciferase reporter assays. Results Bioinformatic screening highlighted Ninj1 as a prominently upregulated candidate transcript post-ICH, a finding corroborated by robust induction in both in vivo and in vitro hemorrhagic models. title: Resting-State Hyper- and Hypo-Connectivity in Early Schizophrenia: Which Tip of the Iceberg to Focus On?
abstract: Purpose We examine brain connectivity alterations in early-stage schizophrenia, with a focus on patterns of hyper- and hypoconnectivity. Although altered functional connectivity (FC) is well documented in schizophrenia, substantial inconsistencies remain regarding the location and direction of specific dysconnections. We hypothesize that early FC changes in schizophrenia include both decreases and increases and are correlated with symptoms and medication levels, with insufficient preprocessing potentially masking out some of these effects. Method Using a large sample of 100 first-episode schizophrenia patients (42 females) and 90 healthy controls (50 females), we compared FC across 90 brain regions defined by the Automated Anatomical Labeling atlas. We assessed medication effects and examined associations between FC changes and duration of untreated psychosis, duration of antipsychotic (AP) treatment, and symptom severity. In addition, we performed a systematic comparison of four functional magnetic resonance imaging data denoising strategies. Finding Relative to controls, patients showed increased FC in 150 region pairs and decreased FC in 15 pairs, when using a "stringent" data denoising scheme. Despite this numerical imbalance, the overall distribution of FC changes remained balanced: Median FC was not systematically shifted, indicating no global bias toward hyper- or hypoconnectivity. Importantly, several FC alterations were significantly associated with symptom severity and AP medication. Conclusion These findings indicate localized dysconnections embedded within a globally balanced connectivity profile in early schizophrenia. This balance was disrupted by less stringent denoising, leading to results dominated by hypoconnectivity, highlighting preprocessing as a major source of variability across studies.

title: Analysis of Invasion Patterns in Occult Involvement Cases of Olfactory Neuroblastoma Using Anatomically Oriented Surgical Specimens.
abstract: Objective Accurate preoperative evaluation of tumor extension in olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB) is critical for optimizing surgical planning, particularly for predicting unexpected intracranial and contralateral invasion. However, discrepancies between preoperative imaging and postoperative pathology remain a challenge. This study compares preoperative imaging with detailed pathological evaluation of anatomically oriented specimens to assess ONB progression, characterize patterns associated with unexpected invasion, and improve surgical strategies. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 58 ONB patients who underwent endoscopic transnasal resection at Jikei University Hospital between January 2018 and March 2024. Preoperative computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging were reviewed by a radiology specialist and compared with postoperative pathological evaluation of anatomically oriented resected specimens. Tumors were classified using Kadish staging and Hyams grading. Results The cohort had a median age of 53 years (range, 29-85 years), with 67.2% male participants. Preoperative staging classified 37.9% of the cases as Kadish C. Among 36 cases preoperatively staged as Kadish A or B, eight (22.2%) exhibited occult intracranial involvement. Unexpected contralateral invasion was observed in five cases, all Kadish C, frequently associated with tumor progression through bony transition areas at the skull base and nasal septum junction. Tumor invasion into the crista galli was identified in six cases, with one case suggesting metastatic spread rather than direct invasion. Conclusions Occult intracranial involvement in Kadish A and B cases may warrant consideration of skull base resection even in early stages. Contralateral invasion was limited to Kadish C and may support consideration of bilateral skull base resection in selected cases where preoperative imaging demonstrates intracranial extension and tumor proximity to key skull base transition areas. Preserving crista galli integrity during resection facilitates detailed pathological evaluation and may contribute to more accurate staging and prognostic assessment.

title: Association of High-Grade Components < 20% on DFS in Stage I Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Real-World Study of Risk Analysis and Predictive Nomogram Development.
abstract: Objective To assess whether high-grade components occupying < 20% of the tumor have prognostic value and whether an Adjusted Grade nomogram improves risk stratification in Stage I invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 1539 patients with pathologically confirmed Stage I invasive LUAD undergoing R0 resection; 1321 with follow-up, including 967 with preoperative CT. Tumors were classified by IASLC Grade and reclassified according to predominant pattern and high-grade components; Adjusted Grade 3 was subdivided into MHGC ≤ 5%, DHGC > 5% to < 20%, and SHGC ≥ 20%. Cox models identified DFS predictors. Nomograms were internally validated with 1000 bootstrap resamples and assessed for discrimination, calibration, and net benefit. Results During a median 38-month follow-up, 124 DFS events occurred. Adjusted Grade 3 independently predicted recurrence (HR 3.07, 95% CI 1.54-6.12), while MHGC and DHGC were associated with poorer DFS (HR 3.95, 95% CI 1.53-10.15; HR 2.55, 95% CI 1.12-5.80). In the CT subgroup, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR) independently predicted DFS (HR 3.08, 95% CI 1.46-6.51). Optimism-corrected C-index was 0.740 for the Adjusted Grade-based nomogram, compared with 0.727 for the IASLC-based nomogram and 0.612 for TNM staging. After adding CTR, they were 0.763 and 0.745 for the Adjusted Grade- and IASLC-based nomogram. Decision-curve analysis showed similar net benefit profiles for the two nomograms. Conclusion High-grade components below 20% were associated with poorer DFS. The Adjusted Grade-based nomogram improved internal discrimination versus IASLC Grade and TNM staging but showed no clear clinical-benefit advantage over IASLC Grade. External validation is needed to establish optimal thresholds and clinical utility.

title: CT-Derived Body Composition Enhances Risk Prediction for Early Progression and Platinum Resistance in High-Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Background Patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) who develop resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy experience significantly poorer outcomes and shorter progression-free survival (PFS). This study evaluates whether pretreatment CT-based abdominal body composition is associated with platinum resistance and PFS, and whether its incorporation alongside clinical variables improves prognostic model performance. Methods This retrospective study included 321 patients with HGSOC (mean age 65 ± 10 years; 28.0% platinum-resistant) treated with platinum-based chemotherapy between 2011 and 2023. Deep learning algorithms quantified abdominal body composition features from pretreatment CT scans, including skeletal muscle, bone, subcutaneous (SAT), visceral (VAT), and intramuscular (IMAT) adipose tissues. Platinum resistance, defined as disease progression during therapy or within 6 months of the final infusion, was the primary outcome. PFS was analyzed as a secondary outcome using Cox proportional hazards modeling. Analyses were stratified by chemotherapy sequence (neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant). Survival models incorporating clinical and CT-derived features were evaluated using 10-fold cross-validated time-dependent AUC over a 5-year follow-up window to predict PFS. External validation was partially performed in an independent cohort of 58 patients with HGSOC. Results Increased SAT and IMAT and decreased skeletal muscle density were independently associated with platinum resistance, with high SAT remaining significant in both the internal and external cohorts (p < 0.05). High adiposity and low muscle density were similarly associated with shorter PFS. Survival models combining clinical and CT-derived features consistently outperformed clinical-only models across all evaluated model classes. The Elastic Net Cox regression model incorporating both feature sets achieved the highest AUC of 0.704 (95% CI: 0.660-0.748). Conclusions Pretreatment CT-derived abdominal body composition is independently associated with platinum resistance and PFS in HGSOC, and its incorporation into predictive clinical models improves discrimination. Body composition assessment may help identify patients at increased risk of platinum resistance and early disease progression.
