title: Detection of recurrence after surgical treatment for urachal adenocarcinoma: diagnostic yield of cystoscopy, imaging and serum tumor markers.
abstract: Purpose Recurrence after surgical treatment of urachal adenocarcinoma (UrAC) occurs in up to 60% of patients, yet evidence-based surveillance strategies are lacking. We evaluated, which diagnostic modality first detected local and distant recurrence after surgery for UrAC and determined their yield to inform evidence-based follow-up. Methods We identified 65 consecutive patients from our prospectively maintained database (1994-2022) who were surgically treated with partial or total cystectomy. Routine follow-up up to 10 years consisted of cystoscopy, serum tumor-markers (STMs - CEA and/or CA19-9) and CT-scan according to our institutional protocol. Diagnostic yield was calculated as the number of recurrences detected until first recurrence divided by the number of examinations performed. Results Of the 65 patients, 33 (51%) developed a recurrence. Isolated local recurrence occurred in four patients (6%), while 29 patients (45%) developed distant recurrence. Recurrence was first detected by symptoms in 39% of patients and by routine follow-up in 61%. Routine cystoscopy detected local recurrence in 2 of 304 examinations; Both patients had simultaneous distant recurrence. For distant recurrence, CT and STMs detected recurrence first in 38%(11/29) and in 28%(8/29) patients, respectively. Conclusion Recurrence after surgery for UrAC is common and predominantly distant. Cross-sectional imaging and STMs contribute most to recurrence detection, whereas routine cystoscopic surveillance rarely detected isolated local recurrence.

title: Super-pulsed thulium fiber laser-assisted retrograde intrarenal surgery is a viable alternative to supine and prone percutaneous nephrolithotomy for solitary 20-30 mm renal stones: clinical outcomes, efficacy, and safety analysis.
abstract: Objective Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) is currently considered the standard treatment for renal stones measuring 20-30 mm. However, recent advances in thulium fiber laser (TFL) technology have expanded the role of retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) in the management of larger stone burdens. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of super-pulsed thulium fiber laser (SP-TFL)-assisted RIRS, supine PCNL (BS-PCNL), and prone PCNL (P-PCNL) for the treatment of solitary renal stones measuring 20-30 mm. Materials and methods This retrospective study included patients who underwent surgical treatment for solitary renal stones measuring 20-30 mm at our institution between January 2020 and March 2026. A total of 260 patients were included: 65 underwent BS-PCNL, 117 underwent prone PCNL, and 78 underwent SP-TFL-assisted RIRS. The primary outcome was the stone-free rate, assessed by low-dose computed tomography (CT) one month after surgery. Secondary outcomes included operative time, hemoglobin decrease, length of hospital stay, and perioperative complications. Results Baseline demographic and stone-related characteristics were comparable among the three groups. Operative time was significantly longer in the prone PCNL group (92.4 ± 22.7 min; p < 0.001). The first postoperative day stone-free rates were 87.6%, 92.3%, and 78.2% in the BS-PCNL, prone PCNL, and RIRS groups, respectively (p = 0.016). However, no significant difference was observed in the final stone-free rates on the one-month CT evaluation (92.3%, 93.2%, and 89.7%, respectively; p = 0.686). Hemoglobin decrease was significantly lower in the RIRS group (3.2 ± 2.8, 2.9 ± 2.6, and 0.5 ± 0.4 g/dL; p < 0.001). Patients who underwent RIRS also had a shorter hospital stay (1.44 ± 0.77, 1.36 ± 0.68, and 1.12 ± 0.49 days; p = 0.008). Intraoperative and postoperative complication rates were comparable across the three groups. Conclusion SP-TFL-assisted RIRS represents a safe and effective alternative to PCNL for solitary renal stones measuring 20-30 mm. Although early postoperative stone-free rates were lower than those achieved with PCNL, comparable one-month stone-free rates, lower blood loss, and shorter hospitalization suggest that SP-TFL-assisted RIRS may represent an effective alternative to PCNL in appropriately selected patients.

title: Too good to be true? AI performance in CT-based urinary stone detection and classification: EAU endourology systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate pooled performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in computed tomography (CT)-based urinary stone detection and classification and identify methodological factors influencing results. Methods This review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261319940). A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted up to March 15, 2026. Studies evaluating AI-based detection or classification of urolithiasis on CT with available validation/test cohort data (sensitivity/specificity or 2 × 2 tables) were included. A bivariate random-effects model generated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) curves. Meta-regression explored moderators related to dataset composition and AI pipelines. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-AI. Results 14 studies (five detection-based, nine classification-based) were included. Overall pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.967 and 0.979 (AUC 0.987). Classification studies demonstrated higher pooled sensitivity (0.977) and specificity (0.990) compared with detection studies (0.935 and 0.919; AUC 0.945). Significant heterogeneity was observed and influenced by training sample size, class imbalance, presence of bladder stones or other pathologies, and architectural choices. Most studies had high risk of bias, lacked external validation, and frequently used slice-level or pre-selected datasets, potentially overestimating performance. Conclusion Substantial methodological heterogeneity and high risk of bias limit clinical generalizability. Detection studies better reflect real-world workflows and show lower performance. Current evidence does not support routine clinical implementation without standardized reporting and robust external validation.

title: Non-transecting posteriorly augmented anastomotic ureteroplasty with lingual mucosal onlay grafts: 5-year multi-institutional experience in 52 cases.
abstract: Purpose Complex proximal or mid-ureteral strictures remain a reconstructive challenge, especially in patients with complete obstruction. We aimed to evaluate the short- to mid-term feasibility, safety, and efficacy of non-transecting posteriorly augmented anastomotic ureteroplasty with lingual mucosal onlay grafts (ntPAA-LMGU). Methods In this retrospective, multicentre study, we reviewed adults who underwent robot-assisted ntPAA-LMGU at three centres and had at least 6 months of follow-up. Primary surgical success required the absence of symptoms, the absence of radiographic evidence of recurrent stricture, and freedom from secondary intervention. Renal functional outcomes were assessed by changes in overall estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and serial eGFR values were analysed using a linear mixed-effects model. Results The procedure was completed robotically in all 52 patients. Ten patients (19%) had previously undergone ureteral reconstruction. Median stricture length was 3.0 cm (IQR 2.9), median graft length was 3.0 cm (IQR 2.0), and median graft width was 1.5 cm (IQR 0.3). Median operative time was 167 min (IQR 75), median estimated blood loss was 50 mL (IQR 30), and median postoperative hospital stay was 6 days (IQR 2). No open conversion or intraoperative complications occurred. At a median follow-up of 17 months (IQR 13), the renal functional success rate was 94% (49/52), and the surgical success rate was 94% (49/52). Postoperative complications occurred in six (12%) patients, including two Clavien-Dindo grade IIIa events. Conclusions ntPAA-LMGU is a safe, feasible, and effective reconstructive option for complex proximal or mid-ureteral strictures.

title: Molecular diagnostics and liquid biopsy approaches in diffuse midline glioma: an update and literature review.
abstract: Purpose Diffuse midline gliomas (DMGs), H3 K27-altered, are aggressive childhood central nervous system tumors that remain almost uniformly fatal. Historically diagnosed radiographically as diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), these tumors are now defined by integrated anatomic and molecular criteria encompassing H3 K27-mutant, EZHIP-overexpressing, and EGFR-altered subtypes. Advances in tissue sampling have transformed understanding of their molecular landscape, but their eloquent location, the sampling bias inherent to stereotactic biopsy, and the impracticality of repeated tissue sampling have motivated interest in biofluid-based approaches. Liquid biopsy is being investigated as a complementary modality for molecular characterization, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of progression and resistance. Methods A narrative review of the literature was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE for articles published through 31 July 2026, supplemented by a ClinicalTrials.gov search performed on the same date. Eligible articles described liquid biopsy methodologies, biomarker substrates, or clinical applications in DMG or DIPG; a separate, explicitly labeled category of enabling or methodologically relevant studies performed on tissue or in other tumor types was retained. Results We summarize the WHO CNS5 molecular definition of DMG, the role and limitations of tissue-based diagnosis, the spectrum of liquid biopsy substrates and platforms with study-level performance data, and the incorporation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sampling into interventional DMG trials. We distinguish exploratory biomarker collection from analytically or clinically validated testing, and we address CSF access, safety, selection bias, and turnaround time. Conclusions Liquid biopsy in DMG remains investigational. No application, whether molecular diagnosis, response monitoring, pseudoprogression adjudication, or treatment adaptation, is currently prospectively validated for clinical decision-making. Standardized, prospective, multi-institutional studies with predefined thresholds are required.

title: Long-term (≥ 10-year) outcomes after laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Purpose To the best of our knowledge, no previous dedicated study has evaluated laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision (LCCE) in a cohort in which all patients had at least 10 years of follow-up. We therefore evaluated long-term outcomes after LCCE in this population. Methods This retrospective two-center cohort study included all 47 consecutive eligible children who underwent LCCE between June 2009 and September 2016. All patients had at least 10 years of confirmed follow-up. The standardized technique included cyst excision with tailored intrapancreatic dissection, intraoperative endoscopy of the common channel and/or intrahepatic ducts, and mucosa-to-mucosa Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy (HJ). The primary endpoint was late biliary event-free survival; overall late event-free survival including intestinal events was a secondary endpoint. Results Ten patients (21.3%) had at least 15 years of follow-up. Median follow-up was 12.85 years (IQR 10.89-14.64; range 10.00-17.26). Early and first-year complications occurred in 8 (17.0%) and 4 patients (8.5%), respectively. Two patients (4.3%) developed qualifying late biliary events: one developed cholangitis at 1.02 years and was treated medically, and the other developed an intrahepatic stone at 5.14 years and underwent redo reconstruction. Late biliary event-free survival was 95.7% at both 10 and 15 years. One additional patient underwent surgery for adhesive intestinal obstruction at 13.79 years, resulting in an overall late event-free survival of 90.4% at 15 years. No late pancreatitis, clinically relevant remnant duct pathology, internal hernia, or biliary malignancy occurred. Conclusions Standardized LCCE was associated with durable long-term biliary outcomes. However, late biliary and intestinal complications remained possible, supporting continued surveillance into adulthood.

title: Forearm osteochondromas in the paediatric population with multiple hereditary exostoses-a scoping review.
abstract: Introduction Forearm osteochondromas in the paediatric population can cause progressive deformity, functional impairment, growth disturbance, and cosmetic concerns. This scoping review aims to map and synthesise the contemporary evidence on the natural history, classification, and management of forearm osteochondromas in the paediatric population with multiple hereditary exostoses (MHE). Methods Four databases: MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane were systematically searched for studies reporting on forearm osteochondromas in the paediatric population. Eligible studies included forearm osteochondromas with MHE in patients aged under 18 years reporting on natural history, classification or outcomes following any intervention. Two authors independently screened titles and abstracts, followed by the full-text review of potentially eligible studies. Disagreements regarding eligibility were resolved by a third reviewer. Data were extracted and synthesised descriptively. Results Twenty-eight studies were included. Most studies evaluated radiographic and functional outcomes of surgical interventions (n = 20). Eight observational studies (non-interventional studies) assessed other objectives, including classification systems, natural history, and risk factors for radial head dislocations. The Masada classification system was the most utilised for MHE (n = 17), while others used Jo or Gottschalk classifications. Current MHE classification systems are not sufficient for guiding management. Radiographic parameters may assist in identifying forearms at higher risk of radial head dislocation, such as increased radial shortening, ulnar shortening, radial blow, radial articular angle and the presence of distal and greater ulna osteochondromas. These findings are most evident on anteroposterior radiographs of the forearm. Conclusion Clinical decision-making should take into account both functional outcomes and radiographic findings, not just the classification systems such as Masada classification. Gradual ulnar lengthening is the most commonly reported surgical intervention, with bone healing potentially improved by adjunct intramedullary fixation. Lower body mass index and smaller ulnar diameter likely predispose to delayed healing. Future research should prioritise developing a reliable classification system that guide management.

title: Intraoperative non-contact three-dimensional measurement of the facial recess using a 4K3D exoscope during cochlear implantation.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the technical feasibility of 4K3D exoscope-based non-contact three-dimensional measurement of the facial recess and explore agreement with scale-calibrated two-dimensional ImageJ measurements in cadaveric specimens and preoperative CT measurements in patients undergoing cochlear implantation. Methods The system used in this study combined an AINNOVI-100 exoscope with SurgeReal 3D Studio. Cadaveric feasibility assessment and method comparison included 10 temporal bones from eight formalin-fixed cadaveric heads. Three-dimensional measurements were compared with scale-calibrated two-dimensional ImageJ measurements. The prospective single-center cohort included 23 patients undergoing cochlear implantation. Intraoperative measurements were compared with preoperative high-resolution computed tomography measurements for exploratory agreement using absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Cadaveric intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.878 to 0.934. Mean model-generation time was 1.97 s, and the recorded workflow from reconstruction initiation to result storage lasted 46.07 s. 31 of 35 cadaveric measurement attempts were successful (88.6%), including 29 initial successes (82.9%); 4 attempts failed (11.4%). In the 23 clinical cases, agreement was strongest for facial recess width (intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.962). Angular limits of agreement were wider but remained within the stated ± 10° comparison margin in both cohorts. Conclusion This study supports the feasibility of obtaining non-contact quantitative measurements of the exposed facial recess using a 4K3D exoscope. The observed agreement, particularly for facial recess width, and the short reconstruction and measurement times support further evaluation of this workflow for intraoperative anatomical documentation. Future studies should establish three-dimensional measurement accuracy and reproducibility and examine how the resulting information contributes to surgical decision-making.

title: Perilymphatic enhancement suggestive of blood-labyrinthine barrier dysfunction in tumor-negative unilateral asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss on 10-minute postcontrast 3D heavily T2-weighted FLAIR MRI.
abstract: Purpose We hypothesized that a subset of patients with tumor-negative, nonacute unilateral asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss (ASNHL) would show occult perilymphatic enhancement suggestive of blood-labyrinthine barrier (BLB) dysfunction on 10-min postcontrast three-dimensional (3D) heavily T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (hvT2-FLAIR) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This study aimed to determine its detection rate and regional distribution. Methods This retrospective study included 25 adults with nonacute unilateral ASNHL who underwent 3-T inner-ear MRI after post-imaging exclusion of three vestibular schwannomas from 28 clinically eligible patients. Precontrast 3D FLAIR, precontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR, and 10-min postcontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR images were visually scored. Expert-reviewed automated segmentation generated regional normalized signal intensity (NSI), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and contrast-enhancement percentage (CEP). Results Postcontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR showed definite asymmetric perilymphatic enhancement in 15 of 25 patients (60%), significantly exceeding precontrast 3D FLAIR (8%; p < 0.001) and precontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR (16%; p = 0.002). Inter-reader agreement was nearly perfect (κ = 0.915). The affected ear exhibited higher NSI and CNR in the basal turn and vestibular complex, and CEP was higher only in the basal turn; these findings remained significant after false discovery rate correction. We hypothesized that a subset of patients with tumor-negative, nonacute unilateral asymmetric sensorineural hearing loss (ASNHL) would show occult perilymphatic enhancement suggestive of blood-labyrinthine barrier (BLB) dysfunction on 10-min postcontrast three-dimensional (3D) heavily T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (hvT2-FLAIR) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Postcontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR showed definite asymmetric perilymphatic enhancement in 15 of 25 patients (60%), significantly exceeding precontrast 3D FLAIR (8%; p < 0.001) and precontrast 3D hvT2-FLAIR (16%; p = 0.002). title: The orbito-pterygo-sphenoidal ligament/posterior septal artery complex as a dual-function anatomical reference for transethmoidal sphenoidotomy.
abstract: Introduction The superior turbinate and sphenoid ostium are commonly used landmarks for sphenoidotomy; however, they may be obscured in severe inflammatory conditions such as eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS) or affected by anatomical variations. This study evaluated the orbito-pterygo-sphenoidal ligament/posterior septal artery (OPSL/PSA) complex-guided transethmoidal sphenoidotomy (TES) as an anatomy-based approach for sphenoid sinus entry and controlled inferior extension of anterior sphenoid wall (ASW) removal. Methods This retrospective study included patients with ECRS who underwent sphenoidotomy. Outcomes were compared between the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group (24 patients, 48 sides) and a conventional group (25 patients, 50 sides). The primary endpoint was postoperative residual inferior ASW height measured using computed tomography. Secondary endpoints included ASW width, intraoperative events, operative time, and postoperative exploratory outcomes. Results Postoperative residual inferior ASW height was significantly smaller in the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group than in the conventional group (-0.8 ± 1.8 vs. 1.5 ± 2.5 mm; p < 0.001). The difference remained significant after adjustment for potential confounders. Superior turbinate resection was not performed in the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group, whereas it was performed in 28.0% of sides in the conventional group. No statistically significant differences in operative time or PSA-related hemorrhage were observed between groups. Conclusions The OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES was associated with a greater extent of inferior ASW removal and less frequent superior turbinate resection, with no statistically significant differences in operative time or ​PSA-related hemorrhage between groups. The OPSL/PSA complex may serve as a complementary anatomical reference with a dual function: assisting sphenoid sinus entry and guiding controlled inferior ASW removal in patients with ECRS.

title: Pretreatment total gross tumor volume complements TNM staging in predicting survival in locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the prognostic significance of pretreatment gross tumor volume (GTV) and determine whether volumetric assessment provides additional prognostic value beyond conventional TNM staging in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. Methods This retrospective study included 124 patients treated with definitive radiotherapy between 2012 and 2024; 117 received concurrent systemic therapy. Pretreatment GTVprimary, GTVnodal, and GTVtotal were measured on planning CT for patients treated with upfront radiotherapy and on the CT component of pre-induction PET/CT for patients receiving induction chemotherapy. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine cutoff values. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. The incremental prognostic value of volumetric parameters was assessed using Akaike's Information Criterion (AIC)-based model comparison. Results The selected cutoff value for GTVtotal was 36 cc. Although GTVprimary showed the highest AUC in ROC analysis, GTVtotal remained associated with disease-specific survival after multivariable adjustment and yielded the lowest AIC among the compared models. Patients with GTVtotal > 36 cc had poorer disease-specific survival. GTVtotal, T stage, and age > 60 years were independently associated with disease-specific survival. Conclusion Pretreatment GTVtotal provides complementary prognostic information beyond conventional TNM staging and may improve risk stratification in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. The data-derived cutoff requires external validation before clinical use. The 36-cc threshold may be influenced by the predominance of hypopharyngeal tumors in the high-volume group and should be applied cautiously to laryngeal cancer cohorts.

title: Multiparametric morphometric analysis of free flaps in head and neck oncologic surgery.
abstract: Introduction Free flap reconstruction has become the gold standard after major oncologic resections in the head and neck (HN) region. Despite advances in techniques, free flaps undergo volumetric and structural changes over time, potentially compromising functional and aesthetic outcomes. This study aims to explore a solid three-dimensional method to perform multiparametric assessment of free flaps. Methods and materials A cohort of 32 patients undergoing ablative HN surgery followed by free flap reconstruction was studied, using postoperative CT/MRI scans at fixed intervals. Semi-automatic 3D segmentation was adopted to measure soft tissue flap parameters, excluding bone. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses examined dimensional changes, separating fasciocutaneous and muscular components. Results Cross-sectional analysis showed significant dimensional variability among anatomical subsites, particularly in the volume and thickness of fasciocutaneous components. Longitudinal data revealed that muscular flap components underwent significantly greater reductions in diameter, surface area, and volume compared to fasciocutaneous tissue, which remained relatively stable over time. No significant differences in dimensional changes were observed between different flap types overtime. Conclusion This study presents a reproducible 3D methodology for multiparametric assessment of free flaps in HN reconstruction. The marked reduction in muscular components relative to fasciocutaneous tissues highlights the importance of considering differential shrinkage in surgical planning and potential overcorrection. Future prospective studies with larger cohorts and earlier imaging are needed to validate and optimize reconstructive strategies.

title: Sex estimation in a Malaysian population using radiographic measurements of the femur and humerus.
abstract: Sex estimation plays a vital role in forensic anthropology, particularly in the identification of unknown human remains. Thisstudy investigates sexually dimorphic traits in radiographic images for the purpose of estimating biological sex. Specifically, measurements of the femur and humerus were analysed, as these long bones exhibit significant sexual dimorphism. A total of 200 individuals were included in this study. X-ray images of the femur and humerus were obtained from the Department of Radiology, Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM), Malaysia. The dataset included demographic information such as age, sex, and individuals of Malay, Chinese, and Indian population group. Measurements of the epicondylar breadth (EB) and vertical head diameter (VD) of both the femur and humerus were recorded. Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) was applied to evaluate the effectiveness of these measurements for sex estimation. The results demonstrated that the combination of two bone parameters achieved an overall classification accuracy exceeding 85% in sex estimation. These findings highlight significant morphological differences between males and females and provide a statistically robust approach for sex estimation in a Malaysian population.

title: Predictive modeling of sex from proximal femoral morphometry using machine learning algorithms: a radiological study in Egyptian adults.
abstract: Sex estimation is a foundational step in forensic identification, and the proximal femur, whether assessed through direct skeletal measurement or radiographic imaging, has shown considerable promise as a durable, sexually dimorphic anatomical region for this purpose. Machine learning (ML) classifiers offer a flexible alternative to traditional discriminant function analysis, yet Egyptian data combining radiographic proximal femoral morphometry with supervised ML remain limited. Hence, this study aimed to develop and compare ML models for sex estimation from proximal femoral radiographic measurements in an adult Egyptian population. Digital pelvic radiographs of 306 Egyptian adults, 135 males and 171 females, aged ≥ 30 years, were retrospectively analyzed. Four proximal femoral measurements, femoral head diameter, femoral neck axis length, femoral neck width, and intertrochanteric distance, were obtained after confirming bilateral symmetry. Nine supervised algorithms were trained and evaluated using cross-validation together with an independent hold-out test set, with performance assessed through accuracy, F1-score, and receiver operating characteristic analysis. All four measurements differed significantly between sexes, with femoral head diameter showing the largest effect size and emerging as the dominant predictor across most models. The decision tree classifier achieved the highest test-set accuracy at 86% (F1-score = 0.83), followed by the multilayer perceptron at 83% (F1-score = 0.82), although sex-specific accuracy revealed nontrivial classification bias for most models, with only gradient boosting and AdaBoost remaining within the 5% bias threshold generally considered acceptable in forensic practice. Area under the curve values ranged between approximately 0.85 and 0.91 on the test set. These findings suggest that proximal femoral radiographic measurements, and femoral head diameter in particular, may offer a reliable and population-specific basis for ML-assisted sex estimation in Egyptian adults. However, sex-specific performance, not accuracy alone, should guide the choice of any model intended for forensic application.

title: Feasibility of reducing Angiofil ® concentration in multiphase postmortem CT angiography and implications for iodine consumption and environmental sustainability : an observational study.
abstract: Background Postmortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is widely used in forensic medicine to evaluate the vascular system before autopsy. The contrast mixture of 3,500 ml paraffin and 210 ml Angiofil ® , originally proposed by Grabherr et al. for multiphase postmortem CT angiography (MPMCTA) approach, provides reliable global vascular opacification. Recent advances in CT detector technology, image reconstruction techniques, and growing environmental concerns have encouraged the investigation of alternative contrast-agent dilutions aimed to reduce iodine consumption. The aim of this observational study was to explore whether lower Angiofil ® concentrations could be used while preserving adequate vascular visualization and diagnostic image quality. Methods Thirty cases were evaluated using four progressively diluted Angiofil ® -paraffin mixtures containing 200 ml, 180 ml, 150 ml, and 120 ml of Angiofil ® in 3,500 ml of paraffin. Contrast enhancement was quantified by measuring Hounsfield units (HU) within regions of interest (ROIs) placed in the ascending thoracic aorta and compared with a clinical case. Image quality was independently assessed by an experienced forensic radiologist based on opacification of the ascending thoracic aorta. In addition, a dedicated evaluation of coronary artery lumen and wall visualization was performed. Results The mixture containing 200 ml of Angiofil ® showed no relevant improvement in image quality compared with the original dilution. A mixture containing 180 ml of Angiofil ® allowed excellent vascular assessment in individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m², whereas 150 ml of Angiofil ® provided optimal image quality in individuals with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m². The contrast mixture of 3,500 ml paraffin and 210 ml Angiofil®, originally proposed by Grabherr et al. for multiphase postmortem CT angiography (MPMCTA) approach, provides reliable global vascular opacification. The aim of this observational study was to explore whether lower Angiofil® concentrations could be used while preserving adequate vascular visualization and diagnostic image quality.

Thirty cases were evaluated using four progressively diluted Angiofil®-paraffin mixtures containing 200 ml, 180 ml, 150 ml, and 120 ml of Angiofil® in 3,500 ml of paraffin. Image quality was independently assessed by an experienced forensic radiologist based on opacification of the ascending thoracic aorta. In addition, a dedicated evaluation of coronary artery lumen and wall visualization was performed.

The mixture containing 200 ml of Angiofil® showed no relevant improvement in image quality compared with the original dilution. A mixture containing 180 ml of Angiofil® allowed excellent vascular assessment in individuals with a BMI > 35 kg/m², whereas 150 ml of Angiofil® provided optimal image quality in individuals with a BMI ≤ 35 kg/m². title: Semi-automated sex estimation from the cochlea on routine clinical CT: limited incremental value of curvature-based shape descriptors.
abstract: Background Sex estimation is fundamental in forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology, yet classical methods rely on skeletal elements that are often absent or poorly preserved. The bony labyrinth, enclosed within the petrous bone, is a promising alternative owing to its early maturation and taphonomic resistance, and cochlear shape has been reported to carry a sex-specific signal. However, most approaches depend on manual segmentation, micro-CT, or complex shape-analysis frameworks that limit routine applicability. Objective To evaluate the feasibility of a semi-automated method for sex estimation from the cochlea using standard clinical CT and automated OTOPLAN segmentation, and to quantify the contribution of shape descriptors beyond cochlear size alone. Materials and methods We analyzed 139 cochleae from 87 adults using clinical CT scans (slice thickness ≤ 0.6 mm). The three-dimensional lateral wall path was extracted with OTOPLAN; after normalization and resampling, curvature- and torsion-based descriptors and scalar cochlear metrics were computed to train a supervised classifier. Preprocessing, feature, and hyperparameter choices were optimized by Bayesian optimization within a nested cross-validation, so that model selection and performance estimation used separate data. Six feature configurations were compared, with all partitions made at the patient level and the whole procedure repeated over five random partitions. Results In nested cross-validation, the best configurations reached an area under the ROC curve (AUC-ROC) of approximately 0.71. A model using cochlear diameter as its sole predictor did not differ detectably from those combining size and shape descriptors (AUC-ROC 0.71, 95% CI 0.62-0.80) and gave the highest balanced accuracy (0.70), with a sensitivity of 0.71 and a specificity of 0.70. Configurations restricted to shape descriptors reached a median AUC-ROC of 0.59, with lower confidence limits at or just above chance level (0.50-0.51). Adding curvature to diameter changed the median AUC by + 0.011 (95% CI - 0.064 to + 0.107). Conclusion Sex-related information is recoverable from cochlear geometry on routine clinical CT using a semi-automated pipeline, but no incremental value of shape descriptors beyond cochlear size was detected. Although accuracy remains moderate, the approach is non-destructive, scalable, and clinically compatible, offering a potential adjunct for forensic anthropology and bioarchaeology when conventional methods are unavailable. This is not an identification method and is not validated as a stand-alone forensic tool: it was evaluated by internal validation only, on in vivo clinical CT.

title: Development and technical validation of a standardised CT image preprocessing workflow for reproducible AI for forensic anthropological applications.
abstract: The use of computed tomography (CT scans) images is increasing in forensic anthropology to address ethical, logistical, and preservation challenges related to physical cadaveric collections. However, preparing large volumes of medical images for artificial intelligence (AI) applications remains challenging, particularly in terms of standardisation and data privacy. The aim of this study is to develop an automated preprocessing workflow for CT images to support machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) applications in forensic anthropology research and education. Methodology A Python-based pipeline was designed in three stages: data de-identification and sorting, patient table removal, and bone windowing. A script was developed for de-identification, and a custom U-Net architecture was developed for both patient table removal and bone windowing. The workflow was developed and applied to CT thorax. Model performance was evaluated using standard metrics and compared with ground-truth models. Results DICOM metadata de-identification was performed as part of preprocessing; all predefined identifying attributes were successfully processed in the 200 DICOM files examined. The patient table removal model removed the table successfully in 96% of datasets (192/200) and achieved 99.94% accuracy on the original, non-augmented test images. The bone segmentation model achieved a Dice score of 93.12% and a precision of approximately 90%. The segmented 3D models showed high agreement with the ground-truth model, with minimal geometric deviation. Conclusions We have proposed an integrated workflow that provides an ethical, efficient and standardised solution for de-identifying and preprocessing CT imaging data. It also enables the preprocessing of a scalable dataset for AI applications, thereby supporting the development of methodologies for the modern population, with future expansion to full-body scans and other imaging modalities.

title: Post-mortem CT angiography for fatal vascular lesions in forensic death investigation: a systematic review of diagnostic performance, added value, and pitfalls.
abstract: Purpose Post-mortem CT angiography (PMCTA) is increasingly used in forensic death investigation to assess vascular disease, haemorrhage, and traumatic or natural vascular causes of death. However, its practical value depends on the lesion being investigated, the angiographic protocol, and the way imaging findings are integrated with autopsy and pathology. This systematic review evaluated the diagnostic performance, added value, and main pitfalls of PMCTA for fatal vascular lesions. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane/CENTRAL were searched for human post-mortem studies evaluating PMCTA in forensic, medico-legal, coronial, or post-mortem settings. Eligible studies compared PMCTA with autopsy, histopathology, targeted vascular dissection, or autopsy-based consensus. Evidence was grouped according to practical forensic use, including coronary stenosis assessment, autopsy triage, global vascular lesion detection, haemorrhage-source localization, aortic or traumatic vascular injury assessment, coronary plaque characterization, and artifact-related pitfalls. Risk of bias was assessed using a QUADAS-2-based approach adapted to forensic PMCTA studies. Results The available evidence did not support unrestricted pooling of all fatal vascular lesions. PMCTA was used for different forensic questions, and only coronary stenosis provided data close to conventional diagnostic accuracy assessment. In this domain, available studies showed high specificity but only moderate sensitivity for critical stenosis. Autopsy-triage studies suggested that PMCTA may reduce or guide invasive autopsy in selected adult coronial workflows. Global comparison studies showed added value for vascular lesion detection, and haemorrhage-source studies suggested that PMCTA may help localize bleeding vessels. Evidence on fatal coronary plaque characterization is emerging. Pitfall studies showed that post-mortem clots, incomplete vascular filling, contrast leakage, and extravasation artifacts may mimic or obscure vascular pathology. Conclusion PMCTA is best interpreted as a complementary tool in forensic vascular death investigation rather than as a general substitute for autopsy. Its contribution is strongest when it answers a specific vascular question, such as documenting coronary stenosis, guiding autopsy, mapping vascular lesions, localizing haemorrhage, or supporting targeted histopathology. Careful correlation with autopsy, pathology, case circumstances, and protocol-related artifacts remains essential.

title: Automated whole-dentition CBCT phenotyping enables explainable sex classification and age estimation through distinct dental features.
abstract: Tooth size and morphology are established primarily during development, whereas secondary dentin deposition and pulp-space remodeling continue throughout adulthood, providing biologically distinct information for sex and age estimation. This study investigated whether automated whole-dentition cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) analysis could capture these two signals. The initial cohort comprised 327 adult CBCT scans, of which 275 passed automated segmentation-completeness screening and entered the final analysis (141 female and 134 male participants; age range, 21-61 years). ToothSeg was used for automatic tooth segmentation and numbering. After excluding variables potentially reflecting image acquisition rather than dental biology, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models were developed separately for sex classification and age regression. Performance was assessed using five-fold out-of-fold predictions, and feature importance was interpreted using SHAP. The sex model achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.807 and an AUC of 0.872, while the age model achieved a mean absolute error of 5.29 years and an R² of 0.645. Lower-right canine volume was the most important individual feature for sex classification and was greater in males (Cohen's d = 1.20). Mean incisor relative low-gray voxel fraction was the most important age feature and was inversely correlated with chronological age (Spearman ρ = -0.706). As an exploratory study, automated whole-dentition CBCT phenotyping showed internally predictive, biologically interpretable patterns for adult sex and age estimation. However, given the modest sample size and proxy low-gray metric, multicenter external and anatomical validation are required.

title: Fetal age estimation using micro-CT volumetric and metric analysis of deciduous tooth germs.
abstract: Background Accurate estimation of fetal age underlies the determination of legal viability and associated forensic and clinical decisions. Deciduous tooth germs are early-forming, resistant structures previously used for age estimation via two-dimensional linear measurements, but no study has provided an in situ volumetric quantification of their constituent tissue compartments. This study aimed to estimate fetal age from microCT-derived metric and volumetric measurements of deciduous tooth germs across wide gestational range. Method Thirty fetal specimens (11 weeks - 23 weeks) from the Dutch Fetal Biobank were stained with (B-)Lugol's solution and scanned by microfocus-computed tomography. Deciduous tooth germs were segmented into three tissue compartments (mineralized tissue, dental papilla, peripheral tissue). Volume, height, width and thickness were recorded for each germ. Age-estimation models were compared at several levels of aggregation (individual germ, bilateral pair, dental quadrant, tooth type, total dentition), using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), with nested cross-validation to account for model selection and 95% prediction intervals for individual estimates. Left-right asymmetry, mineralization chronology, and intra-observer reproducibility were also assessed. Results The bilaterally averaged height of the maxillary central incisor estimated gestational age with R² = 0.971 and LOOCV RMSE = 0.74 weeks (95% prediction interval ± 1.5 weeks), comparable to a composite total-volume model (R² = 0.962, LOOCV RMSE = 0.83 weeks), which remained usable when teeth were missing or unsegmentable. Accounting for model selection by nested cross-validation, the expected error was 0.92 weeks. Femoral diaphyseal length measured on the same specimens performed comparably (LOOCV RMSE = 0.61 weeks). Mineralization onset followed a consistent tooth-specific sequence without a consistent lead of either arcade. Conclusion Micro-CT provides the first in situ volumetric description of the tissue compartments of the human fetal deciduous tooth germ. In this exploratory cohort, a simple linear measurement, maxillary central incisor height, estimated gestational age with a precision that warrants its evaluation as a complement to skeletal indicators in post-mortem fetal imaging, pending external validation.

title: In vivo assessment of brain microstructure in patients with Huntington's disease using quantitative MRI.
abstract: Objectives Using multiparametric mapping (MPM), we assessed the integrity of cortical and subcortical regions across different stages of Huntington's disease (HD), relating the derived findings to genetic modifiers and clinical measures. Methods Sixteen premanifest patients with HD (PwHD pre ), ten manifesting PwHD (PwHD man ), and forty-two healthy controls (HC) underwent clinical examinations and a 3 T imaging. We derived quantitative MPM maps to perform voxel-based quantification (VBQ) and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). We assessed group differences by combining PwHD pre and PwHD man (PwHD total ) and by comparing PwHD pre and PwHD man with age- and sex-matched HC. Using correlation analysis, we investigated the link between MPM-derived findings, CAG repeat length, and clinical scores. Results PwHD man presented with reductions in all four quantitative MPM maps across the bilateral caudate nucleus and the frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital gyri. We observed spatial overlap between VBQ- and VBM-derived findings, demonstrating widespread volume loss in PwHD man . PwHD pre showed reductions in certain quantitative maps within the frontal and temporal regions. Reduced MPM values correlated with clinical scores of HD severity. Interpretation The observed reductions across four MPM modalities in PwHD man are consistent with demyelination and neuronal loss, as supported by widespread volume loss. The reductions observed in PwHD pre indicate early demyelination and inflammation. In this study, we demonstrated the utility and clinical relevance of MPM for detecting microstructural alterations across different stages of HD. MPM can serve as a non-invasive biomarker of neurodegeneration in HD, providing insight into the pathological events underlying the observed neuronal loss.

title: Thirteen-month real-world effectiveness and safety of lecanemab in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease: integrating objective clinical outcomes and caregiver-reported experiences.
abstract: Background The longer-term real-world effectiveness of lecanemab and predictors of treatment response remain unclear in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD). Methods This prospective multicenter cohort enrolled patients receiving lecanemab (10 mg/kg biweekly) across nine medical centers in Southwest China. Longitudinal cognition, 13-month amyloid-β positron emission tomography/computed tomography (Aβ-PET/CT), safety, treatment discontinuation, and caregiver-reported Clinical Global Impression (CGI) outcomes were assessed. Cognitive trajectories were compared with propensity score-matched local controls and an external Alzheimer's disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) natural-history cohort. Results Among 122 lecanemab-treated patients, 38.52% had mild cognitive impairment due to AD and 40.98% had mild AD dementia. Linear mixed-effects models incorporating 222 follow-up visits demonstrated generally stable cognitive performance, with modest favorable changes in cognitive scores at certain follow-up time points. At 13 months, 84.00% maintained or improved Clinical Dementia Rating stage, and 66.67% achieved amyloid-negative conversion, defined as a Centiloid value < 12. Lecanemab-treated patients showed more favorable longitudinal cognitive trajectories than matched ADNI and local natural-history controls. Amyloid reduction was not robustly associated with cognitive improvement, and routine baseline clinical variables did not reliably predict treatment response. CGI assessments indicated clinical improvement or stability in 77.55% of participants. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities and infusion-related reactions occurred in 10.66% and 5.74% of patients, respectively, while treatment discontinuation was most commonly driven by the inconvenience of repeated infusions rather than safety concerns. Conclusion Lecanemab was associated with favorable longitudinal cognitive trajectories, substantial amyloid clearance, and acceptable safety in Chinese patients with AD. However, amyloid reduction and routine baseline clinical characteristics did not reliably predict treatment response.

title: Comparative evaluation of GPT 5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro large multimodal models for retinal optical coherence tomography interpretation.
abstract: Purpose Large multimodal models (LMMs) capable of interpreting medical images are increasingly accessible to patients, yet their reliability for retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) interpretation remains uncertain. This study evaluated the performance of two state-of-the-art LMMs in detecting OCT features and generating diagnostic interpretations. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 330 publicly available retinal OCT B-scans spanning 12 diagnostic categories, including normal scans and common retinal diseases, were analyzed. Two commercially available LMMs (GPT 5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro) were evaluated using zero-shot inference. Models were assessed separately for detection of nine predefined OCT features and for free-text diagnostic interpretation. Feature detection performance was measured using per-feature metrics and macro-averaged F1 scores, while diagnostic accuracy was assessed against expert-adjudicated reference standards. Results Gemini 3 Pro demonstrated higher feature detection performance than GPT 5.2 Pro (macro-averaged F1 score 0.558 vs. 0.472) and higher diagnostic accuracy (58.8% vs. 32.1%). Both models performed better for visually salient abnormalities but showed limited sensitivity for subtle structural features. Normal OCT scans were frequently misclassified as pathological, particularly by GPT 5.2 Pro, which failed to correctly identify any normal images. Recurrent, model-specific diagnostic biases and hallucinated diagnoses were observed. Conclusions Although LMMs can extract clinically relevant information from OCT scans, their diagnostic reliability remains limited, with frequent overcalling of pathology and systematic biases. Given their increasing availability to patients, these limitations raise concerns about potential misinterpretation outside supervised clinical settings. Careful validation and clear usage boundaries are needed before such tools can be safely integrated into patient-facing workflows.

title: The integral role of artificial intelligence models in retinal detachment diagnostics: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose Retinal detachment (RD) is a vision-threatening condition requiring prompt diagnosis and management to optimize visual outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models have demonstrated promising results in RD detection across multiple imaging modalities; however, concerns regarding heterogeneity, external validation, and real-world implementation remain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical applicability of AI models for RD diagnostics. Methods A comprehensive electronic search of PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP), and Google Scholar was conducted in April 2026. Studies evaluating ML or DL models for RD detection, classification, segmentation, screening, or prognostic assessment using any imaging modality were included. Two independent reviewers performed study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment using the QUADAS-2 and CLAIM tools. Quantitative syntheses were performed using a bivariate random-effects model to pool sensitivity and specificity, while a random-effects inverse-variance model was applied for diagnostic odds ratio (DOR). Subgroup analyses were conducted according to imaging modality and use of external validation status. Publication bias and small-study effects were assessed using Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test. Results Sixty-six studies were included in the systematic review, of which 31 studies comprising 118,432 images were eligible for meta-analysis. Fundus photography was the most commonly used imaging modality, and DL approaches predominated. The pooled sensitivity was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.89-0.95) and specificity was 0.98 (95% CI: 0.96-0.99), with moderate between-study heterogeneity. The model-based positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were 0.86 (95% CI: 0.71-0.94) and 0.99 (95% CI: 0.97-1.00), respectively. The SROC curve yielded an AUC of 0.982 and a normalized pAUC of 0.964, while the pooled DOR was 642.3 (95% CI: 264.5-1559.7). No significant publication bias or small-study effects were detected (P = 0.544). Conclusions This study provides the most up-to-date comprehensive quantitative synthesis of AI applications for RD diagnostics, demonstrating excellent overall diagnostic performance across multiple imaging modalities. Despite these promising results, limited external and real-world clinical validation, together with methodological heterogeneity, continue to restrict clinical translation. Future multicenter prospective studies with standardized validation and reporting frameworks are essential for safe and generalizable implementation of AI-assisted RD diagnostics.

The model-based positive predictive value (PPV) and negative predictive value (NPV) were 0.86 (95% CI: 0.71-0.94) and 0.99 (95% CI: 0.97-1.00), respectively. The SROC curve yielded an AUC of 0.982 and a normalized pAUC of 0.964, while the pooled DOR was 642.3 (95% CI: 264.5-1559.7). No significant publication bias or small-study effects were detected (P = 0.544).

Conclusions

This study provides the most up-to-date comprehensive quantitative synthesis of AI applications for RD diagnostics, demonstrating excellent overall diagnostic performance across multiple imaging modalities. Despite these promising results, limited external and real-world clinical validation, together with methodological heterogeneity, continue to restrict clinical translation. Future multicenter prospective studies with standardized validation and reporting frameworks are essential for safe and generalizable implementation of AI-assisted RD diagnostics.

title: Neuroendocrine neoplasms of the digestive system: challenges of biopsy diagnosis.
abstract: The diagnosis of digestive neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) is increasingly being made on endoscopic biopsies and endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration/biopsy (EUS-FNA/FNB) or ultrasound biopsies taken from metastases. Although current classification systems provide a robust and elaborate framework for categorizing NENs, their application to limited tissue biopsy samples often remains challenging. A major challenge is the accurate distinction between well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) and poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs), which is essential because of their markedly different prognostic and therapeutic implications. Additional challenges include reliable Ki-67 assessment, recognition of intratumoral heterogeneity, and identification of mixed neoplasms, including mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) and amphicrine-like carcinoma (ALC)-a recently introduced and still poorly characterized category-and assignment of the primary site in metastatic disease using organ-associated immunohistochemical markers. Site-specific differences in morphology and immunophenotype further complicate biopsy interpretation and require integration of histological, immunohistochemical, clinical, and radiological findings. Although morphology remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, molecular testing is increasingly used in difficult cases to identify predictive biomarkers and potentially actionable genomic alterations. This review focuses on a practical biopsy-oriented diagnostic approach, discusses major diagnostic pitfalls, controversial and emerging concepts, and highlights the clinicopathological features of NENs across the digestive tract.

title: A multi-subject tractography atlas of human cerebellar connections.
abstract: The cerebellum is a highly interconnected structure involved in motor coordination and balance as well as cognitive, sensory, autonomic, and emotional functions. Its connectivity relies on complex afferent and efferent white matter pathways linking it with the brainstem, spinal cord, thalamus, cerebral cortex, vestibular system, and limbic-related structures. Recent advances in diffusion MRI (dMRI) and tractography have enabled the in vivo reconstruction of these pathways, offering new opportunities to study cerebellar anatomy and connectivity. However, compared with supratentorial white matter, cerebellar connections remain underexplored owing to their smaller size, anatomical complexity, and the absence of comprehensive tractography atlases. We propose a white matter tractography atlas of candidate cerebellar white matter pathways, consistent with previously reported neuroanatomical descriptions based on regions of interest (ROIs) derived from 30 young healthy volunteers from the Human Connectome Project (HCP). A total of 22 ROIs were segmented to reconstruct, via tractography, 19 cerebellum-associated tractography components, comprising eight bilateral pathways (16 hemisphere-specific reconstructions), and the three major cerebellar white matter conduits: the superior, middle, and inferior cerebellar peduncles (SCP, MCP, and ICP). The eight bilateral pathways comprise the cerebello-ponto-hypothalamic, parieto-ponto-cerebellar, fronto-ponto-cerebellar, occipito-ponto-cerebellar, contralateral cerebello-thalamo-cortical, dentato-rubro-thalamo-cortical, dorsal spinocerebellar, and periaqueductal gray-cerebellar pathways. The delineation of some anatomical regions, particularly the olivary nucleus and the hypothalamus, presented methodological challenges. Difficulties in reliably reconstructing the olivocerebellar pathway led to its exclusion from the final atlas. Two independent neuroanatomical experts evaluated the 19 atlas tracts using four qualitative criteria, finding good anatomical fidelity with overall mean scores of 3.9 and 3.8 out of 5, respectively. The same reconstruction procedure was then applied to 25 additional HCP participants to evaluate the automatic segmentation of these bundles in unseen participants. The proposed atlas provides a framework for studying putative cerebellar structural connectivity, acknowledging that tractography-derived streamlines represent inferred white matter pathways rather than direct evidence of synaptic connections or axonal trajectories and its relationship with motor and non-motor functions. It enables quantitative tractometry analyses derived from diffusion MRI models and facilitates the integration of multimodal and functional information. This atlas may support future research in neuroscience, neuropsychiatric disorders, and neurosurgical planning by providing a standardized representation of cerebellar white matter pathways.

title: Microstructural alterations of human medial temporal lobe in dementia: volumetric and DTI findings correlate with cell number and neuropathology.
abstract: Volumetric and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) alterations in medial temporal lobe (MTL) regions are consistently reported in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, their biological basis remains poorly understood. We combined Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) metrics with cellular quantification and neuropathological burden assessment to investigate microstructural substrates underlying MTL imaging alterations in human donors with known cognitive and neuropathological status. Absolute cell numbers were quantified in a cohort of 54 brain donors using the isotropic fractionator, and postmortem MRI was performed on a subset of 18 fixed brain hemispheres. To assess microstructural brain alterations associated with disease progression, in vivo volumetric and DTI metrics were analyzed in 39 cognitively unimpaired controls (CU), 31 individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 14 patients with clinical AD dementia. In the postmortem cohort, MTL diffusivity metrics showed moderate negative correlations with total cell numbers. Mean, axial, and radial diffusivity positively correlated with Braak stage, whereas fractional anisotropy (FA) correlated negatively with CERAD score, linking diffusion alterations to AD-related pathology. In vivo MTL analyses revealed increased mean, axial, and radial diffusivity, and reduced FA in AD patients compared with both CU and MCI individuals. The MCI group exhibited intermediate alterations in diffusivity. Differences between in vivo and postmortem diffusion values were consistent with tissue fixation, temperature, and variations in acquisition protocols. Our findings suggest that diffusion MRI alterations in the MTL are associated with reduced cellularity and neuropathological burden, supporting the biological relevance of DTI metrics as markers of microstructural degeneration in AD.

title: The unfolding symphony: unraveling brain dynamics via data-driven multi-scale functional connectivity in task-state fMRI.
abstract: Task-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) can characterize both regional responses and changes in statistical dependence among distributed brain systems. This narrative review examines dynamic and multiscale connectivity within a broader framework that distinguishes task-modulated functional connectivity, trial-wise covariation, effective connectivity, and data-driven state analysis. Sliding-window correlation, hidden Markov models, and co-activation patterns are compared by their data representations, temporal assumptions, and computational procedures; graph representations can be combined with each of these strategies. We discuss supervised recurrent, transformer, and graph models alongside unsupervised state discovery, self-supervised representation learning, and emerging brain foundation models. Explainability requires evaluation of model attributions, including graph masks and perturbation-based analyses, rather than anatomical plausibility alone. The spatial framework includes whole-brain networks, subnetworks, atlas-defined regions of interest, and voxel- or layer-level measurements. Proposed links across these levels remain hypotheses: faster sampling of the blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) signal does not directly resolve millisecond neural interactions, and resting-state or animal findings do not establish the corresponding mechanism during human tasks. Shared task-evoked responses, hemodynamic variability, motion, and analytical choices can all alter apparent connectivity. Progress therefore depends on matching the estimator to the scientific question, comparing against activation and static-connectivity baselines, and validating results across participants, sessions, and acquisition settings.

title: Associations between peripheral immune markers and brain morphometry in normal individuals.
abstract: Peripheral immune signaling may be associated with brain structure, but evidence in healthy adults remains limited. We conducted a cross-sectional exploratory study to examine associations between circulating immune-marker concentrations and regional cortical morphometry. Structural T1-weighted MRI and peripheral blood samples were obtained from 62 healthcare workers. Cortical volume, surface area, thickness, and mean curvature were extracted for 68 Desikan-Killiany regions using FreeSurfer. Nine peripheral immune markers were measured. Associations were assessed using Spearman rank correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction across 34 regions within each immune-marker, hemisphere, and morphometric-measure family. Associations surviving false discovery rate (FDR) correction in the analyses were further examined using exploratory sensitivity general linear model adjusted for age, sex, and the corresponding global morphometric measure (estimated total intracranial volume for volume and total cortical surface area for surface area). TGF-β1 was the only immune marker with regional associations surviving FDR correction. Higher TGF-β1 concentrations were positively associated with right frontal cortical surface area (Spearman's ρ = 0.367-0.443) and volume (ρ = 0.345-0.502), involving caudal middle frontal, rostral middle frontal, superior frontal, lateral orbitofrontal, and pars orbitalis regions. Exploratory covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses yielded nominal p-values below 0.05 for right caudal middle frontal surface area (β = 1.609) and volume (β = 4.914), and right superior frontal surface area (β = 2.740) and volume (β = 10.939). No associations involving cortical thickness, mean curvature, or other immune markers survived FDR correction. In this pilot exploratory study of apparently healthy adults, peripheral TGF-β1 concentrations were associated with regional variation in right frontal cortical surface area and volume. These cross-sectional findings do not establish causality, underlying mechanisms, functional relevance, or clinical significance, but provide preliminary hypotheses for larger longitudinal studies of peripheral immune-brain associations.

title: Monitoring of pulmonary outcomes in paediatric cystic fibrosis patients treated with modulator therapy-a narrative review.
abstract: Recently introduced CFTR modulator drugs have transformed the disease trajectories in people with cystic fibrosis. Children with cystic fibrosis, who would once have experienced progressive lung damage and pulmonary function decline from early life onwards, now, when treated with effective modulators, appear to have preserved lung structure and pulmonary function using conventional monitoring tools. However, since cystic fibrosis lung disease may still progress despite effective therapy, early detection of disease manifestation, disease progression, and the tracking of treatment responses remain crucial. Monitoring of lung disease in the current era of CFTR modulators, therefore, poses a fundamental challenge for cystic fibrosis clinicians and researchers. This narrative review summarises currently available monitoring tools for paediatric cystic fibrosis patients. Conclusion In children with cystic fibrosis receiving effective CFTR modulator therapy, spirometry remains an important component of pulmonary monitoring but may be insufficient to detect early or residual lung disease. Complementary approaches, including multiple-breath washout, oscillometry, and structural and functional lung imaging, can provide more sensitive assessment of pulmonary abnormalities and treatment responses. Further development of sensitive, non-invasive biomarkers of airway infection and inflammation, alongside evidence to guide the integration of these tools into routine clinical care, remains an important priority. What is known • CFTR modulator therapy has transformed clinical outcomes in cystic fibrosis, and children initiating effective modulators early in life frequently maintain normal or near-normal pulmonary function. • Conventional monitoring with spirometry, particularly FEV₁, has limited sensitivity for detecting early or residual cystic fibrosis lung disease. What is new • Clinical monitoring of cystic fibrosis lung disease in children has shifted towards the use of technologies allowing for detection of subtle, potentially reversible, structural, functional, and inflammatory abnormalities that may persist despite modulator therapy. • Multiple-breath washout, quantitative computed tomography (CT), functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the chest, as well as emerging biomarkers provide complementary information beyond spirometry and are reshaping contemporary monitoring of CF lung disease.

Children with cystic fibrosis, who would once have experienced progressive lung damage and pulmonary function decline from early life onwards, now, when treated with effective modulators, appear to have preserved lung structure and pulmonary function using conventional monitoring tools. In children with cystic fibrosis receiving effective CFTR modulator therapy, spirometry remains an important component of pulmonary monitoring but may be insufficient to detect early or residual lung disease. Complementary approaches, including multiple-breath washout, oscillometry, and structural and functional lung imaging, can provide more sensitive assessment of pulmonary abnormalities and treatment responses. What is known

• CFTR modulator therapy has transformed clinical outcomes in cystic fibrosis, and children initiating effective modulators early in life frequently maintain normal or near-normal pulmonary function. • Conventional monitoring with spirometry, particularly FEV₁, has limited sensitivity for detecting early or residual cystic fibrosis lung disease.

What is new

• Clinical monitoring of cystic fibrosis lung disease in children has shifted towards the use of technologies allowing for detection of subtle, potentially reversible, structural, functional, and inflammatory abnormalities that may persist despite modulator therapy. • Multiple-breath washout, quantitative computed tomography (CT), functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the chest, as well as emerging biomarkers provide complementary information beyond spirometry and are reshaping contemporary monitoring of CF lung disease.

title: Theory of mind, autism-like traits, executive functions, and structural brain MRI findings in children with neurofibromatosis type 1.
abstract: This study aimed to examine social-cognitive difficulties in children with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) by jointly investigating theory of mind (ToM), executive functions, and autism-like traits and to explore whether children with NF1 show structural differences in brain regions commonly implicated in social cognition and executive functioning. In this two-center cross-sectional study, 41 children aged 8-18 years were included, comprising 21 children with NF1 and 20 age- and sex-matched typically developing children. Participants underwent behavioral assessment, including parent-reported autism-like traits, everyday executive functioning, and direct measures of ToM. Structural brain MRI data were analyzed using automated volumetric and cortical thickness measures, focusing on these regions. Children with NF1 showed higher autism-like traits, lower everyday executive functioning in play and social routines, and poorer performance on an advanced ToM task. The NF1 group also had larger global brain volume reflecting widespread white matter expansion; lower cortical gray matter proportion and thickness in frontal, temporal, parietal, cingulate, and limbic regions; and larger subcortical structures including the amygdala, hippocampus, and thalamus.
